Verified against the real source tree (560 of 764 package functions are unreachable from the two entry points).

This spec was caught by its own predecessor's drift at /dev-next time: its authored worked-example fixture (ledger/prompt.py:build_standing_items_section) had been deleted by [spec 0257.1](specs/0257.1-delete-dead-legacy-standing-items-surface.md), so it was retargeted onto run_phase1 (a still-on-disk dead legacy runner) during reconcile.

summary: Raiser self-ADDRESSes its own already-addressed items (spec 0257.2).
items: Raiser self-ADDRESSes its own already-addressed items ([spec 0257.2](specs/0257.2-raiser-addressed-no-self-address-prohibition.md)).
The group-3 standing-items instruction (_RAISER_ADDRESSED_INSTRUCTION in orchestrator/deep_research.py) listed the ratify ops (RESOLVE / ACKNOWLEDGE / counter-argue) but never prohibited ### ADDRESS.

When a raiser's item flips open → addressed it moves from group 2 to group 3 and lost the no-self-address prohibition group 2 carried, so the raiser reached for ### ADDRESS again — the raiser_self_address violation (5× in live run 20260530-205144-spec-0257-validation, all phase 2 / round 3 / agent claude; the ops were dropped and did not block convergence).
The fix adds the prohibition (and surfaces the already-legal ### WITHDRAW op) to the group-3 instruction, mirroring the group-2 wording.
Prompt-text-only steering change — no code path, partition logic, verifier invariant, lifecycle edge, or event type changes.

summary: Dead legacy standing-items prompt surface (spec 0257.1).

summary: Role-aware standing-items surface (spec 0257).
items: Added. Role-aware standing-items surface ([spec 0257](specs/0257-phase2-role-aware-standing-items-addressee-obligation.md)).

The per-round standing-items block agents see in phase 2 / phase 4 is now grouped by (role, lifecycle-state), so each agent sees only the operations legal for it: items raised against it under a *you-are-the-ADDRESSEE, you MUST ADDRESS* group; its own open items under a *do-not-self-address / no-resolve-from-open* group; its own addressed items under a *ready-to-ratify* group (with addressed_by surfaced).

New format_role_aware_standing_items in orchestrator/deep_research.py; both live render sites (dr_run._format_standing_items and DeepResearchPhase._build_standing_items_text) route through it, so there is exactly one role-aware surface.

Standing role-contract callouts in the live _v2 prompt builders. _ADDRESS_RESOLVE_ROLE_CALLOUT (symmetric raiser/addressee) renders above ## Status in plan_negotiation_round1_prompt_v2 / plan_negotiation_round_n_prompt_v2; a distinct _ADDRESS_RESOLVE_ROLE_CALLOUT_PHASE4 (asymmetric drafter/reviewer wording, per cowork correction 3) renders in review_round1_prompt_v2 / review_round_n_prompt_v2.

summary: Apply-time anchor failures in the phase-4 drafter-delta path no longer kill the run (spec 0256).
items: Added. Apply-time anchor failures in the phase-4 drafter-delta path no longer kill the run ([spec 0256](specs/0256-drafter-delta-apply-guard-resync-and-strict-anchor-contract.md)).

On the captured live run 20260529-164844-backend-language-choice the drafter's round-3 EDIT_SECTION ops anchored on multi-line body + table-row literals against a draft that had diverged (round-2 no-op'd, so on-disk draft-v2.md lacked the edits the drafter believed it had made).
apply_revised_draft_deltas raised edit_section_anchor_not_found *outside* the parse-only fallback, propagated to the run-level tombstone, and the run died at EXIT_RUNTIME with no final.md.
Three changes ship together:

Changed. The phase-4 drafter prompt no longer leaks a reviewer-style ADDRESS affordance for the drafter's own items ([spec 0256](specs/0256-drafter-delta-apply-guard-resync-and-strict-anchor-contract.md) §2.4).

The evidence run emitted raiser_self_address ×7; the "Addressing items raised against me" / "Ratifying my own items" sections of the round-N prompt now make "ADDRESS targets only the other agent's items; use RESOLVE/ACKNOWLEDGE/WITHDRAW for your own" unambiguous on the drafter path.
The apply-layer drop semantics (raiser_self_address ProtocolViolation) are unchanged.

summary: A fully-agreed phase 2 no longer deadlocks to the hard cap when one agent's AGREED is demoted by the spec-0229 addressee-obligation rule (spec 0255).
items: Fixed. A fully-agreed phase 2 no longer deadlocks to the hard cap when one agent's AGREED is demoted by the spec-0229 addressee-obligation rule ([spec 0255](specs/0255-decouple-closeout-urge-from-effective-status.md)).

On the captured live run 20260529-091956-backend-language-choice both agents emitted byte-identical STATUS: AGREED across rounds 3–8, yet phase 2 ground to its 8-round hard cap, wrote phase2-deadlock.md, exited 51, and produced no final.md (cost: $7.19).

Root cause: openai ADDRESSed only 1 of claude's 6 raised items, so 5 stayed open, openai's AGREED was demoted to an effective IN_PROGRESS every round, and that single demoted status was fed into both end-of-round gates — disarming the closeout → ghost-cap escape valve (0 CloseoutUrged events emitted) along with the convergence gate.
Changed. The closeout-urge gate is decoupled from effective status ([spec 0255](specs/0255-decouple-closeout-urge-from-effective-status.md)).

At both end-of-round assembly sites in deep_research.py (process_round_end — the live run_dr_phase2 path — and the run_round parity path), check_convergence keeps consuming the spec-0229 effective statuses (a demoted AGREED must not *converge*), but should_urge_closeout now consumes the raw self-reported statuses.
Per spec 0114 a demoted AGREED is still a convergence *attempt* — so the demotion no longer also disarms the escape valve.
The phase now arms closeout, spends the per-phase closeout budget, and converges via_ghost_cap (exit 0) instead of dead-ending.
Every spec-0229 mechanism is preserved (the demotion still fires every offending round and still blocks convergence; verifier invariant I2.4 stays gating-green).

summary: A parked spec's RECENT ACTIVITY row now reads "Parked" instead of "QUEUED" (spec 0254).
items: A parked spec's RECENT ACTIVITY row now reads "Parked" instead of "QUEUED" ([spec 0254](specs/0254-parked-spec-activity-event-renders-as-queued.md)).

A parked spec's creation event uses the same queued lifecycle step as a runnable spec, so the dashboard activity feed mislabelled it — e.g. spec 0253.1 showed 08:35:22 UTC · QUEUED · 0253.1 while the Parked lane and queue-picker correctly excluded it.
No new lifecycle event type is introduced (that would be a contract change); the queued step stays the single creation event and the renderers became parked-aware.

items: All-Runs card status no longer diverges from the run-detail status for abandoned runs ([spec 0253](specs/0253-fix-all-runs-card-status-diverges-from-detail.md)).

summary: Added: RemoteSession.push_metrics_only(session_dir) — a single-row update of…
items: Added. RemoteSession.push_metrics_only(session_dir) — a single-row update of just the runs.metrics JSONB column (remote.py), for repair paths that mutate only metrics and touch no events/files/blobs/pieces.

Fixed. backfill-critique --push no longer times out re-uploading whole sessions ([spec 0252.2](specs/0252.2-backfill-critique-metrics-only-push.md)). The --push block in _run_backfill_critique (cli.py) reused the full-session push_session_dir path, whose heavy events/session_files/attachment_blobs/turn_prompt_pieces re-upload exceeded Supabase's statement timeout (57014) on large runs (e.g.
backend-language-choice) — the operator then could not tell whether the backfilled critique_by_agent tally had landed.
The backfill mutates only critique_by_agent inside metrics, so the block now calls push_metrics_only, a single-column runs.metrics update.
Provably sufficient: no derived runs column moves, and the hosted All Runs band reads critique straight from runs.metrics.
recompute-costs --push (which moves cost/duration totals feeding derived columns) is deliberately left on the full-push path — see spec §7.
PATCH bump.

summary: API-key sourcing now reads ~/.zshenv (the file that actually holds the keys), with ~/.zshrc as a fallback.
items: API-key sourcing now reads ~/.zshenv (the file that actually holds the keys), with ~/.zshrc as a fallback. The canonical eval "$(grep … )" recipe and the MissingCredentialError hint strings in cli.py grepped only ~/.zshrc; the keys live in ~/.zshenv, so the command extracted nothing and E2E runs only worked because .zshenv is auto-sourced into every interactive shell — a silent dependency that breaks in any context where .zshenv isn't loaded.
All sites now grep ~/.zshenv ~/.zshrc 2>/dev/null so the tooling is agnostic to which Z-file holds the keys.
Matches the same fix already landed in CLAUDE.md and the dual-research-run skill.

summary: Make the carve-out disposition gate executable in the queue picker (spec 0251).
items: Make the carve-out disposition gate executable in the queue picker ([spec 0251](specs/0251-executable-carve-out-disposition-gate.md)). CLAUDE.md's doctrine — *"a carve-out reaches /dev-next only when its disposition is ship"* — was enforced by nothing; the queue picker filtered on kind == "dev" and status == "queued" only and never read disposition, so an archive/defer carve-out still ran as long as it was queued.
Four coordinated changes close the gap, and the scope expands from carve-out-only to all queued dev specs:

summary: Buffer /dev-next pre-merge telemetry into two batched flushes (spec 0250).
items: Buffer /dev-next pre-merge telemetry into two batched flushes ([spec 0250](specs/0250-dev-next-pre-merge-telemetry-batched-flushes.md)). The pre-merge window of the /dev-next cycle used to push ~8 individual spec(NNNN): queue-state update commits to origin/main (one per --push-to-main lifecycle event across steps 12–17), the dominant source of main-history noise.

It now mirrors the proven post-merge buffering (specs 0212/0247): every happy-path event is emitted local-only and the buffer is flushed in exactly two batched commits — Flush 1 at step 12 (cycle start / in_progress, also making the previously-unfulfilled "committed at step 12" promise for the buffered cycle_started/preflight/reconcile events real) and Flush 2 at step 17 (PR opened).
Net: ~8 pre-merge commits → 2.
No contract change — same events, lifecycle states, and vocabulary; only the origin/main push cadence moves.
Failure writes (semantic drift at step 11, tests red at step 16) keep --push-to-main so a halt stays immediately visible on the dashboard; the post-merge window (steps 18–23) is untouched.

A pure-stdlib source-pattern test (tests/test_spec_0250_dev_next_pre_merge_buffering.py, skip-when-absent guarded) locks the local-only happy path, the exactly-two-flushes shape, and the never-buffer-failures invariant.

summary: Path-filter deploy.yml so only image-affecting commits deploy (spec 0249)..
items: Path-filter deploy.yml so only image-affecting commits deploy ([spec 0249](specs/0249-path-filter-deploy-only-image-affecting-commits.md)). .github/workflows/deploy.yml triggered on every push to main with no paths: filter, so each /dev-next cycle's ~13 queue-state update telemetry commits (touching only dashboard/ and at most handoffs/) fired a full test → flyctl deploy --remote-only → sweep pipeline that shipped a byte-identical image and serialized behind the deploy-main concurrency group.
Added an allow-list on.push.paths scoped to the files that actually change the shipped image (src/**, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile, fly.toml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml).

The allow-list is a superset of the files every spec PR is guaranteed to touch (the CLAUDE.md versioning rule bumps pyproject.toml + src/dual_research/__init__.py), so the merge-commit deploy that /dev-next step 20 watches always fires; workflow_dispatch remains as the manual force-deploy escape valve.
A pure-stdlib YAML-shape regression test (tests/test_spec_0249_deploy_path_filter.py) locks the allow-list shape, the telemetry-path exclusion, and the version-bump-path invariant.

summary: Rich per-provider metric bands on the All Runs cards (spec 0248 §2.5).
items: Added. Rich per-provider metric bands on the All Runs cards ([spec 0248](specs/0248-all-runs-card-refinements-provider-metrics.md) §2.5). The raised/solved tallies are computed at run-write time and persisted under metrics.json's new critique_by_agent key (AgentBreakdown gains tokens / searches / critique fields; Metrics gains critique_by_agent); the cheap /api/runs list path reads the persisted payload and never replays transcripts (a summarize_run cheap-path guard test enforces this).
Old runs without the payload render zero tallies.

Same archive/restore endpoints.

Avatar account menu restored to the All Runs chrome ([spec 0248](specs/0248-all-runs-card-refinements-provider-metrics.md) §2.2). AvatarMenu / AvatarDisc / MenuItem are lifted from app.jsx into run-list.jsx (which loads first, so app.jsx's chrome still references them) and mounted in AllRunsChrome in place of the bare initial span — restoring the Google avatar, identity header + admin badge, Design language, Replay tour, Settings, and Sign out.

Changed. All Runs card chrome cleanup ([spec 0248](specs/0248-all-runs-card-refinements-provider-metrics.md) §2.1 / §2.4). The redundant dual-research wordmark strip (ProjectStrip) is removed and .ar-page top padding tightened (24 px → 18 px); the run-card grid now constrains the terminal-state note to the phase-strip (left) column with the provider bands spanning the reclaimed vertical space, rather than a full-width "note note" row.

summary: /dev-next moves the step-18 merged queue-state write to after step 19's force re-detach so it survives to the step-23 atomic flush (spec 0247.1).
items: /dev-next moves the step-18 merged queue-state write to after step 19's force re-detach so it survives to the step-23 atomic flush ([spec 0247.1](specs/0247.1-merged-buffer-survives-step19-force-detach.md)). Spec 0247 made step 18's merged write local-only to close the pre-merge deploy-race, assuming step 23's flush would carry it — but step 19's git checkout --detach -f origin/main force-discards uncommitted working-tree changes to dashboard/queue-state.json, wiping the buffer before step 23 and dropping pr / merged_at / the merged event on every cycle.

Step 18 now only *captures* merged_at at merge time (the MERGED_AT= shell variable, co-located with the spec 0211.2 MERGE_SHA capture); the set status=merged … / append-event … merged *write* relocates to the post-detach buffer cohort (alongside deploy_started / deploy_health_check_ok / handoff_written) that demonstrably survives.
The no-pre-merge---push-to-main property is preserved — the relocated write stays local-only.

Skill-body change (the skill lives outside the repo); the in-repo commit relocates the source-pattern regression guard at tests/test_spec_0247_pre_merge_no_push.py — its antipodal-absence assertions now span step 18 + step 19 — plus this version bump.

items: /dev-next step 18 now buffers the merged lifecycle state locally instead of pushing it to main pre-merge ([spec 0247](specs/0247-pre-merge-push-to-main-deploy-race-hardening.md)). summary: Admin soft-delete on runs (spec 0245).
items: Added. Admin soft-delete on runs ([spec 0245](specs/0245-runs-soft-delete-admin-archive.md)). A hover-revealed archive button on each RunRow (md-icon-btn with , gated on hover && isAdmin && !isArchived && !archivedView) opens a confirmation dialog (Modal Basic variant, error-toned filled Archive button); a POST /api/runs/{id}/archive admin-only endpoint sets deleted_at + deleted_by on public.runs.
A symmetric DELETE /api/runs/{id}/archive restores.

summary: Operational guard: dual-research CLI refuses to run inside Claude Code (spec 0243).
items: Operational guard: dual-research CLI refuses to run inside Claude Code ([spec 0243](specs/0243-operational-guard-refuse-running-inside-claude-code.md)). Routes the user around the H4 silent-kill surface by hard-exiting at the CLI entry when any CLAUDECODE / CLAUDE_CODE_* env var is set, with DUAL_RESEARCH_ALLOW_CLAUDE_P=1 as the documented escape.

Five consecutive Claude-Code-hosted runs (20260527-200213, 20260528-000411/061323/073509/082137) died silently in phase 2–4 with no Python exception, no signal, no jetsam log — root cause: Claude Code's background-task manager terminates long-running children at parent-session lifecycle events; the first plain-Terminal.app run (20260528-094743) completed cleanly ($8.66, 39KB final.md, all gating invariants green).

Layer 1 — CLI guard. New helpers _running_inside_claude_code() and _maybe_refuse_claude_code_host() at src/dual_research/cli.py — detection widens to ANY CLAUDECODE / CLAUDE_CODE_* env var (Cowork sign-off's load-bearing case: the sandbox sets CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_* without CLAUDECODE).

The guard is wired immediately after parser.parse_args(argv) and is conditional on not args.push so the read-only Supabase upload path is exempt; the LLM-firing paths (default --prompt / --brief / --notion + --resume) all hit it before any ingest, cred load, or session-dir creation.
Stderr prints the canonical Terminal.app command with cd to the repo + eval of ~/.zshrc keys + caffeinate -i uv run dual-research; sys.exit(2).
Read-only subcommands (serve, verify, validate-run, recompute-costs, reconcile-costs) are dispatched at the top of main() before the parser ever runs and are not guarded.

Layer 2 — CLAUDE.md "Operational" section. New top-level section after "Tests" documents the canonical Terminal.app invocation and the DUAL_RESEARCH_ALLOW_CLAUDE_P=1 escape's intended use (CI / Cowork sandbox); explicitly NOT intended for "I'm in a hurry, just run it." Layer 3 — /dual-research-run skill amendment. Replaces the "Firing the run" section with a refuse-and-redirect pattern: the skill emits the canonical Terminal.app command for the user to paste rather than firing the run as a Claude Code background task.
Post-run reporting (URLs, completion check) is unchanged.
Layer 4 — --help epilog. dual-research --help now lists DUAL_RESEARCH_ALLOW_CLAUDE_P=1 under an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES section so the escape is discoverable from the tool itself.

Tests at tests/test_spec_0243_claude_code_guard.py cover detection on each of the three env-var families (CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_*), the escape-var allow path + a soft typo guard ("true" still refuses — must be exactly "1"), plain-Terminal allow, main()-level refusal on --prompt and --resume, --push exempt, four read-only subcommand exemptions (verify / serve / validate-run / recompute-costs), --help epilog presence, and source-pattern locks on the CLAUDE.md Operational section + the amended skill.

summary: Per-turn liveness: heartbeat thread + BaseException capture + whole-turn cap wrapping stream consumption; verifier I2.8 (spec 0241).
items: Per-turn liveness: heartbeat thread + BaseException capture + whole-turn cap wrapping stream consumption; verifier I2.8 ([spec 0241](specs/0241-per-turn-liveness-heartbeat-exception-capture-and-stream-wrapping-cap.md)). Closes the per-turn diagnostic gap the runs/20260527-200213-backend-language-choice/ live re-run exposed — phase 4 issued turn_started → turn_inputs then emitted nothing further for ~10 minutes (no turn_ended, no protocol_violation, no tombstone, metrics.json.ended_at = None), and the process was found dead with the user verifying it was not killed.

Two structural gaps allowed the silent death: the existing timeout=600.0 on both AsyncAnthropic and AsyncOpenAI bounds only HTTP request establishment (not mid-stream stalls), and spec 0222's except BaseException tombstone is installed at the run-loop level only — a per-turn API-wrapper exception that escapes via an unawaited task, a stream __aexit__ swallow, or a process-level signal leaves no terminal event.

Layer 1 — heartbeat thread. New module src/dual_research/orchestrator/per_turn_liveness.py exposes HeartbeatThread and the constants TURN_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30 + TURN_WALLCLOCK_CAP_SECONDS = 900.

The heartbeat runs on a separate OS thread (daemon, so a hung join never blocks interpreter shutdown), not an asyncio task — load-bearing because an event-loop block would mute an asyncio-scheduled heartbeat, defeating the diagnostic.
Writes go through the existing Transcript atomic-append; concurrent sibling-turn heartbeats do not corrupt the JSONL (POSIX write(2) on O_APPEND is atomic up to PIPE_BUF).
New TurnHeartbeat(agent, phase, round, elapsed_seconds) dataclass at src/dual_research/events/types.py; written directly to the transcript rather than published through EventBus.

Layer 2 — per-turn except BaseException capture. The wrapper at src/dual_research/orchestrator/_call.py::run_one_call wraps the agent.run await with try/except BaseException and emits a protocol_violation with violation_code="turn_api_call_exception" BEFORE the exception propagates upward to 0222's run-loop tombstone.
Exception-type fidelity is preserved by unwrapping AgentError to its __cause__: an httpx.ReadTimeout re-wrapped as AgentError still surfaces as exception_type=ReadTimeout in the violation reason.
Both events (the per-turn-specific turn_api_call_exception AND the run-loop tombstone) are present in the transcript in the correct order.

Layer 3 — whole-turn wall-clock cap. asyncio.timeout(TURN_WALLCLOCK_CAP_SECONDS=900) wraps the entire agent.run await including stream consumption — distinct from the SDK's 600s request-establishment timeout. 900s gives a 300s margin above the SDK cap so the two never race: a turn_api_call_timeout is unambiguously a stream-consumption stall (the SDK's 600s would have fired first on a request-establishment hang via the Layer 2 path).
The new violation code turn_api_call_timeout is registered in ProtocolViolation's docstring.

Layer 4 — verifier I2.8 (reporting). New _check_i2_8 at src/dual_research/contract/verifier.py (registered immediately after I2.7 in the aggregator) walks the transcript in order, opening on every turn_started and closing on the matching turn_ended / a ProtocolViolation with one of {turn_api_call_timeout, turn_api_call_exception, empty_turn_persistent_identical_input, empty_turn_retry_cap_exceeded} / a tombstone.
Any open turn at end-of-transcript surfaces as an Evidence row pinpointing the bare turn_started.
Reporting-only; promotion to gating is a follow-up spec (§5 §7).

Layer 5 — retry-budget unification. New on_turn_api_call_timeout(state, *, agent, phase, round) at src/dual_research/orchestrator/empty_turn_retry.py ticks the same (agent, phase, round) bucket on_empty_turn does and ALWAYS returns a ProtocolViolation (fail-fast — re-issuing a byte-identical call that just hung 900s would mean back-to-back 15-minute hangs).
The bucket's last_input_sha256 is preserved so a subsequent identical-input empty turn still fail-fasts via the 0239 path.
run_one_call plumbs the unified state from DeepResearchPhase.empty_turn_retry_state (new public accessor) through the dr_run wiring.

Tests at tests/test_spec_0241_per_turn_liveness.py cover all five layers: heartbeat periodicity + survival across a blocked event-loop busy-spin + concurrent-writer atomicity + daemon-thread invariant; the BaseException capture path including KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit / MemoryError / asyncio.CancelledError and the AgentError.__cause__ unwrap; the wall-clock cap firing on a stalled fake agent (monkeypatched cap = 0.1s) + the production-cap constant lock at 900s; eight verifier I2.8 cases (pass for each terminal-counterpart kind, fail for bare turn_started, fail for an unrelated ProtocolViolation that does not count as a terminal, not-applicable on a no-turn transcript, independent-key tracking); and the unified retry-counter helper (single-tick, always-fail-fast, mixed timeout + empty-turn cap unification, per-key independence).
Per spec §2.4 the I2.8 baseline entries are auto-populated by the verifier regen — fixture baselines refreshed via _fixture_regen.regenerate_baseline.

summary: Fixture regen machinery + I2.6 verdict flip on the 142625 + 054652 fixtures (spec 0240).
items: Fixture regen machinery + I2.6 verdict flip on the 142625 + 054652 fixtures ([spec 0240](specs/0240-fixture-regen-machinery-and-i2-6-verdict-flip.md)). Unblocks two named downstream triggers — spec 0232 §6's I2.6 reporting → gating promotion (gated on a 0231/0238-aware regen of the failing fixtures reporting I2.6 = pass) and the spec 0238 §6 verdict-flip line item (the 142625 fixture's I2.6 moves from fail (declared 5, registered 0) to pass once the frozen transcript is regenerated through the post-fix parser).
Layer 1 — new module tests/_fixture_regen.py exposes two callables.

regenerate_transcript(run_dir) walks each raisable phase (0, 2, 4) of run_dir/phase{N}/round-NN-{claude,openai}.md, replays the turn files through parse_turn_v2 + DeepResearchPhase.apply_turn + process_round_end to regenerate the parser-derived event stream (item_raised / item_transitioned / closeout_urged / closeout_violation / protocol_violation / empty_turn_detected), then splices those events back into the captured envelope at each round's last turn_ended boundary.

The original transcript.jsonl is snapshotted to transcript.captured.jsonl on the first call (idempotent — never overwrites an existing snapshot, preserving the immutable evidence consumed by spec 0239's I2.7 integration test on the captured 142625 transcript).

Regenerated parser events carry no ts field — replay has no runtime timestamp and synthesising one would either drift across passes or fabricate a time bracket; the verifier's I5.3 tolerates missing ts on non-terminal events.
regenerate_baseline(run_dir) recomputes expected.json from the live verifier output.

Layer 2 — applied the regen to the two named failing fixtures: tests/fixtures/anchor-runs/20260527-142625-backend-language-choice/ (phase 2 r1 claude now produces 5 item_raised events for the previously-dropped slug-shaped IDs; I2.6 flips fail → pass) and tests/fixtures/anchor-runs/20260527-054652-backend-language-choice/ (phase 2 r1 claude now produces 6 item_raised events; I2.6 flips fail → pass).
The three clean fixtures (010637, 135006, 102321) had their expected.json files refreshed via regenerate_baseline only to backfill the spec 0239 I2.7 invariant entry (transcript.jsonl untouched).

Layer 3 — flipped the snapshot tests in lock-step: test_snapshot_142625_i2_6_slug_drop_fail → test_snapshot_142625_i2_6_post_regen_pass, and the sibling 054652 test, both now assert I2.6.verdict == "pass" against the regenerated baseline.
The legacy regenerate_baseline() at tests/test_verifier.py is preserved as a thin wrapper delegating to _fixture_regen.regenerate_baseline so out-of-tree imports don't break.

Layer 4 — new tests at tests/test_spec_0240_fixture_regen.py cover (a) the post-regen item_raised count on both failing fixtures, (b) idempotency of regenerate_baseline on the three clean fixtures (locks the gating promotion against silent verifier drift), and (c) two-pass byte-identical idempotency of regenerate_transcript + regenerate_baseline on the two regenerated fixtures (locks against silent non-determinism in parse_turn_v2 or apply_turn going forward).

Spec §5: I2.6 promotion from reporting → gating remains a separate follow-up keyed off the next live re-run's I2.6 = pass verdict (non-circular proof; the regen is mildly circular since it replays the post-fix parser over the exact case the fix was built for).

summary: empty_turn_detected retry hardening: identical-input fail-fast + N=2 cap per (agent, phase, round) (spec 0239).
items: empty_turn_detected retry hardening: identical-input fail-fast + N=2 cap per (agent, phase, round) ([spec 0239](specs/0239-empty-turn-detected-retry-cap-and-identical-input-fail-fast.md)). Bounds the orchestrator's retry budget after the 20260527-142625-backend-language-choice live re-run admitted unbounded retry of an empty turn — the prior design at src/dual_research/orchestrator/deep_research.py:760 only appended EmptyTurnDetected events for bookkeeping with no counter gating further retries.

Layer 1 — new module src/dual_research/orchestrator/empty_turn_retry.py defines MAX_EMPTY_TURN_RETRIES=2, the EmptyTurnRetryRecord dataclass, and a pure on_empty_turn(state, *, agent, phase, round, input_sha256) helper that returns a ProtocolViolation on (a) byte-identical retry input — at fixed temperature this cannot succeed — or (b) cap exceeded, else mutates the caller-owned state dict to advance the bucket.
compute_input_sha256(text) is the shared hash helper.

State is owned by the DeepResearchPhase instance (fresh dict per phase invocation) so the reset scope is (agent, phase, round) per Cowork's Ask-3 reasoning — per-run conflates independent turns; per-phase lets an early round drain a later round's budget.

apply_turn at src/dual_research/orchestrator/deep_research.py gains an optional input_sha256: str | None = None kwarg, calls the helper at the empty-turn emission site, and appends the returned violation to the same violations list the orchestrator publishes.
The replay path leaves input_sha256 as None so reconstructed turn replays don't trip the contract.
The production wiring at src/dual_research/orchestrator/dr_run.py hashes the per-turn prompt and threads it to apply_turn.
Layer 2 — EmptyTurnDetected at src/dual_research/events/types.py:572 gains an optional input_sha256: str | None = None field.
ProtocolViolation's docstring registers the two new violation_code values (empty_turn_persistent_identical_input, empty_turn_retry_cap_exceeded).
No migrations — both additions are dataclass fields with defaults.
Layer 3 — new verifier invariant I2.7 at src/dual_research/contract/verifier.py (registered in the aggregator at verifier.py:1267).
Reporting-only initially; promotion to gating gated on a clean reference-run baseline.

The check groups empty_turn_detected events by (agent, phase, round), flags any group whose size exceeds MAX_EMPTY_TURN_RETRIES, and flags any consecutive pair with matching input_sha256 — groups containing a None hash are skipped on the identical-input check so pre-0239 historical fixtures don't false-positive.

Tests at tests/test_spec_0239_empty_turn_retry_hardening.py cover identical-input fail-fast, the N=2 cap, counter reset on round / phase / agent boundary, four I2.7 unit cases (pass / not-applicable / cap-exceeded fail / identical-input fail / None-hash skip), and a live-failure-fix-discipline integration test that runs _check_i2_7 against the captured 20260527-142625 transcript and asserts pass.

summary: Parser primitive consolidation: one tolerant section_heading_re for every specific-literal-heading anchor (spec 0238).
items: Added. Parser primitive consolidation: one tolerant section_heading_re for every specific-literal-heading anchor ([spec 0238](specs/0238-parser-section-heading-primitive-consolidation.md)). Closes the parser-fragility class behind the 2026-05-27 live re-run 20260527-142625-backend-language-choice death — claude's round-1 output glued prose onto the ## New items I'm raising heading (## New items I'm raisingNow I have the evidence I need…), SECTION_NEW_ITEMS_RE's \b terminator failed between g and N, all five ### RAISE blocks were silently dropped, the orchestrator saw an empty turn, fired empty_turn_detected, and burned $3.72 in a retry spin before the user killed it.
Same bug class as spec 0231 at a different surface — 0231 patched extract_fenced_section only; this spec consolidates onto the primitive.
Layer 1 — new public factory section_heading_re(name_pattern, *, flags) compiles ^## (?:\s*$|(?=\S)) with default flags re.MULTILINE | re.IGNORECASE.

The factory takes a raw regex fragment (not an auto-escaped string) so callers needing internal alternation (I'?m, Open questions for.+?, (?:\d+\.\s+)?Open Questions) keep that capability; literal-heading callers use re.escape() themselves.

Layer 2 — eight SECTION_*_RE constants (Stance, Addressing, Ratifying, NewItems, PhaseArtifact, Status, RevisedDraft, CloseoutConstraints) at src/dual_research/contract/markers.py:25-48 rebuilt through section_heading_re; _REVISED_DRAFT_HEADING_RE at src/dual_research/protocol/parse.py:385 re-exported as an alias of SECTION_REVISED_DRAFT_RE so the "Revised draft" anchor cannot drift from the rest of the family; extract_review_items calls section_heading_re(r"Open questions for.+?") and section_heading_re(r"(?:\d+\.\s+)?Open Questions") for its two anchors; extract_fenced_section now calls section_heading_re(re.escape(heading_name)) instead of constructing its regex inline — the two heading-anchor paths share one source of truth.

Layer 3 — explicit scope boundary documented in spec §2.3: _TOP_HEADING_RE, _H2_RE, _DRAFT_SECTION_HEADING_RE are boundary/capture regexes (different abstractions, different roles) and are NOT touched.

Layer 4 — new ### Live-failure fix discipline (spec 0238) section under ## Tests in CLAUDE.md requires every spec whose stated cause-of-death is a captured live-run failure to include at least one test exercising the real entry point of the failing call path against the captured artifact; the spec 0231/0238 mismatch is named as the worked example.

Tests at tests/test_spec_0238_parser_section_tolerance.py cover 11 positive-pattern × clean-heading parametrised cases, 11 antipodal × glued-prose parametrised cases, a 7-shape variant battery on SECTION_NEW_ITEMS_RE (clean / trailing-whitespace / no-apostrophe / ALL-CAPS / trailing-period / trailing-colon+text / glued-letter), an integration test invoking parse_turn_v2 on the captured 20260527-142625 phase-2 round-1 claude turn (asserts both the STATUS-line action array of 5 IDs *and* the 5 RaiseBlocks the bug used to drop), the extract_fenced_section ⇄ SECTION_*_RE shared-source-of-truth match-bounds invariant (spec §7 mitigation), and source-pattern lock-in on the primitive's terminator + default flags.
Full pytest tests/ -q reports 2215 passed (34 new + 2181 pre-existing).
Changed. **SECTION_*_RE family terminator** at src/dual_research/contract/markers.py changed from \b to (?:\s*$|(?=\S)).
The new terminator is strictly more permissive — every heading that matched pre-fix still matches post-fix, plus glued-prose variants now match.
No call site relied on the section *not* matching when prose was glued; the full pytest tests/ -q clean run is the backwards-compat check.
extract_fenced_section at src/dual_research/protocol/parse.py:179 and _REVISED_DRAFT_HEADING_RE at src/dual_research/protocol/parse.py:385 now go through section_heading_re.
Side effect: both pick up re.IGNORECASE (the primitive's default), so headings like ## REVISED DRAFT or ## agreed_plan now match where they previously did not.
This is the consolidation Cowork's brief flagged as "the real structural fix" — extract_fenced_section and the SECTION_*_RE family stop being two heading implementations that can drift.

summary: Verifier invariant I2.6 — STATUS-RAISED-array event cross-check (reporting) (spec 0232).
items: Verifier invariant I2.6 — STATUS-RAISED-array event cross-check (reporting) ([spec 0232](specs/0232-verifier-i2-6-status-raised-event-cross-check.md)). Adds _check_i2_6 directly after _check_i2_5 and registers it in the aggregator block.

For every phase-0/2/4 turn file, the count of IDs declared in the STATUS footer's RAISED_THIS_TURN array is compared to the count of item_raised events scoped to the same (phase, round, raiser) triple.

Directional rule per the 2026-05-27 cowork adjudication: only declared > registered is flagged (the drop class — the 054652 phase-2 r1 claude failure where 6 IDs were declared but 0 events registered, and the 142625 phase-2 r1 claude failure where 5 slug-shaped IDs were declared but 0 events registered).
declared <= registered is benign — OpenAI-style [pending] placeholders or empty arrays standing in for N actual raises do not flag.

summary: Parser heading tolerance + graceful drafter repair fallback (spec 0231).
items: Parser heading tolerance + graceful drafter repair fallback ([spec 0231](specs/0231-parser-heading-tolerance-and-repair-fallback.md)). Closes the parser-strictness failure class behind the live run 20260527-054652-backend-language-choice death — the drafter glued the EDIT_SECTION anchor inline (### EDIT_SECTION ## 1.
Summary), claude glued the phase-2 section heading to prose (## New items I'm raisingNow I have evidence...), and the repair flow's "fix" ablated the substantive edits entirely.

Three layers ship in one bundled commit. (1) _normalise_section_heading at src/dual_research/protocol/parse.py strips a leading markdown H2 token (## ) before the existing numeric-prefix strip, so ## 1.
Summary and 1. Summary both normalise to summary and the drafter's inline-anchor heading argument binds against the draft's ## 1.
Summary section. Standalone-anchor forms (### EDIT_SECTION 1.

Summary) parse identically. (2) extract_fenced_section replaces the trailing \s*$ end-anchor with (?:\s*$|(?=\S)) — either end-of-line (clean form) OR a non-whitespace character lookahead (glued form).

The glued prose becomes harmless preamble in the section body; downstream ### RAISE / ### ADDRESS finders skip over it; the body remains bounded by the next ^## heading outside fenced ranges (per _next_h2_outside_fences).

Partial-prefix false-matches are blocked by the (?=\S) lookahead — ## New items I'm raising does not match heading "New items" because the next char after "items" is whitespace. (3) _apply_drafter_revised_draft — extracted from _on_revised_draft to module level for testability — wraps extract_revised_draft_deltas in a try/except: on ProtocolParseError (i.e., the upstream parse_v2_with_repair couldn't recover after the one-shot repair), the helper synthesises a RevisedDraftFull(content=prior_draft) payload, applies it (producing a byte-equal no-op draft-v(N+1).md), and emits a new ProtocolViolation(violation_code="phase4_drafter_repair_failed", op_kind="revised_draft") event so the deadlock is observable on the dashboard.
The unparseable original is NEVER used as the no-op body — that would ship ANCHOR: / REPLACE_WITH:-shaped garbage downstream.

parse_v2_with_repair at src/dual_research/orchestrator/repair.py gains a drafter exemption from the failures >= 2 exit-52 raise — the round loop continues until hard_cap instead of crashing, with the per-round ProtocolViolation as the audit trail.
Reviewer turns retain the exit-52 path (no fallback for reviewer-side parse failures).
ProtocolViolation docstring gains the new phase4_drafter_repair_failed code entry naming the implementer caution (frequent firing signals layers 2.1/2.2 are too narrow).

New tests at tests/protocol/test_parse.py cover inline EDIT_SECTION + glued-heading parsing positively, standalone-anchor + clean-heading back-compat, partial-prefix non-match, and anchor-fixture replays (10 EditSectionOps from phase4/round-02-claude.malformed-1.md; 6 ### RAISE blocks recovered from phase2/round-01-claude.md).

Integration tests at tests/test_spec_0231_parser_heading_tolerance.py cover the fallback synthesis (byte-equal no-op draft + exactly one ProtocolViolation emission + Phase4DraftRevised advance), clean-turn back-compat (no PV emission on well-formed turns), omitted-section no-op (back-compat), and the parse_v2_with_repair drafter-vs-reviewer exemption split (drafter doesn't raise on 2nd consecutive failure; reviewer still raises).

Out of scope per spec §5: slug-ID normalisation (Finding 3 in the cause-of-death reconciliation); 0228 extension with new violation codes (per Cowork engagement, 0228 is not implementation-incomplete on this evidence — the 18 phase-2 flagged ops are downstream of layer 2.2's registration failure); I2.6 verifier invariant (separate observability spec queued concurrently); repair-prompt copy edits; snapshot updates beyond the anchor fixture.

summary: Added: Addressee-obligation invariant enforced at runtime; verifier…
items: Addressee-obligation invariant enforced at runtime; verifier I2.4 promoted from reporting to gating via a handled-vs-unhandled refactor; CLAUDE.md carve-out-disposition convention codified ([spec 0229](specs/0229-addressee-obligation-invariant.md)). Closes the deeper bug behind the 20260526-102321-backend-language-choice failure — spec 0228 surfaced claude's RESOLVE-from-open ops as ProtocolViolation(resolve_from_non_addressed), but nothing in the protocol compelled openai to ADDRESS items addressed at it before it could emit AGREED; openai's only recourse was ghost-cap, which buried the raiser's items as capped.
The cure is the addressee-obligation invariant from Cowork synthesis §3 Area 2: an agent may not emit STATUS: AGREED while items raised by the OTHER agent remain open and un-ADDRESSed by this agent.

Three layers ship together. (1) Runtime emission in apply_turn — after parsing every turn whose parsed.status == "AGREED", the post-turn ledger is scanned for entries where ent.raiser != agent AND ent.current_state == OPEN; one ProtocolViolation(violation_code="agreed_with_open_addressed_items", op_kind="agreed", expected_state="addressed") per blocking item is appended, naming the raiser and the item id in reason.

The post-turn-ledger scan is deliberate — ADDRESS-then-AGREED in a single turn (ADDRESS flips the item to addressed first, then the check fires against the post-block ledger) is allowed and silent (R1 mitigation). (2) Gate-only demotion via two new fields on RoundResult — effective_claude_status / effective_openai_status — and the _effective_status_for helper that maps AGREED → IN_PROGRESS for any agent with an agreed_with_open_addressed_items violation in this round, passthrough otherwise.
check_convergence, should_urge_closeout, the substantive-convergence escape valve at deep_research.py:1024 AND the production-path equivalent at dr_run.py:478 all consume the effective status.
The agent's self-reported claude_status / openai_status stays on RoundResult for the diagnostic trail; the turn file's STATUS: AGREED line is never rewritten (transcript truth preserved).

No new via_* flag on PhaseConverged — demotion BLOCKS convergence, so no PhaseConverged event is emitted; the via_* partition is the convergence-PATH partition, not the convergence-or-not signal, and the ProtocolViolation event is the complete audit surface explaining why the AGREED didn't count. (3) Closeout-request prompt builder at _build_closeout_request_text now computes two lists — owned_items (raiser == agent, unchanged) and addressed_at_me_items (raiser != agent AND current_state == OPEN) — and passes both to the extended closeout_request_section, which renders a new addressee-obligation block listing each item the agent owes an ADDRESS for with the literal "before declaring AGREED" instruction.
Empty addressed_at_me_items renders nothing (back-compat).

Verifier I2.4 at src/dual_research/contract/verifier.py refactored from a pure-emission detector to a handled-vs-unhandled detector mirroring the spec-0228 I4.4 pattern: every offending AGREED-while-owing turn is classified as either HANDLED (a matching agreed_with_open_addressed_items ProtocolViolation exists for the same (phase, round, agent) scope — the orchestrator demoted the AGREED), UNHANDLED (no matching ProtocolViolation AND a same-(phase, round) phase_converged event exists — the AGREED actually counted toward convergence), or vacuous (no matching ProtocolViolation, no same-round phase_converged — the AGREED didn't count anyway).
UNHANDLED instances fail; the others pass.
Severity flips from reporting to gating.
This refactor is non-optional — a pure severity flip would break healthy post-0229 runs that legitimately contain demoted-and-recovered premature-AGREEDs (the whole point of the demotion mechanism).

ProtocolViolation docstring at src/dual_research/events/types.py:503 extended with a 9th code (agreed_with_open_addressed_items) plus a one-paragraph note explaining it's the runtime counterpart of I2.4.

Three anchor-run baselines at tests/fixtures/anchor-runs/*/expected.json regenerated to record severity: "gating" for I2.4 — the dead primary fixture (20260526-102321-backend-language-choice) flips verdict from reporting/fail to gating/fail (the frozen run's offending AGREEDs are pre-0229, so no matching PVs exist and the round-3 phase_converged event makes them UNHANDLED — the four addressed-at-openai item IDs D-plan-c-02 / D-plan-c-04 / D-plan-c-05 / Q-plan-c-01 named in the evidence list); the clean reference fixture (20260521-010637-dvs-backend-language-choice) flips verdict from reporting/pass to gating/pass (vacuous — no AGREEDs carry open addressed-at-me debt); the dead secondary fixture (20260525-135006-backend-language-choice) verdict follows the same handled-vs-unhandled rule.

CLAUDE.md gains a new "Carve-out follow-ups must triage at carve-out time" subsection nested under "Contract-changing specs are not bugs" — every carve-out spec's frontmatter must include disposition: (ship / defer / archive, default archive) with a one-sentence disposition_reason:.
Validator enforcement of the frontmatter field is deferred to a follow-up under the new convention.

New tests at tests/test_spec_0229_addressee_obligation.py cover: runtime emission with one blocking item produces exactly one ProtocolViolation(agreed_with_open_addressed_items) with the blocking-item id in item_id; ADDRESS-then-AGREED in one turn produces zero such violations; closeout-prompt rendering with both lists populated contains the addressee-obligation block, names each item id, and includes the "before declaring AGREED" string; closeout-prompt rendering with empty addressed_at_me_items omits the block (back-compat); the _effective_status_for helper demotes AGREED to IN_PROGRESS when a matching violation fires and passes through otherwise; verifier I2.4 returns pass (gating) on a transcript with a demoted-AGREED-with-matching-PV; verifier I2.4 returns fail (gating) citing the addressed-at-me item id on a transcript with an AGREED-that-converged-with-owing AND no matching PV; severity flip verified live and in the regenerated baselines for all three anchor-run fixtures.

Out of scope per spec §5: coercing RESOLVE-from-open into WITHDRAW (Cowork synthesis §2.1 deferral); removing ghost-cap / hard-cap as escape valves (the four via_* flags remain a first-class partition); touching _build_standing_items_text beyond the closeout-request builder (Cowork owns the §7.1 blind-spot read of state-presentation); validator enforcement of the new disposition: frontmatter field (deferred to the first follow-up spec carved under the new convention — the test case for itself); backfill / re-classification of pre-1.48.0 runs.

items: apply_turn now emits ProtocolViolation on every state-machine-derived rejection; verifier I4.4 promoted from reporting to gating ([spec 0228](specs/0228-emit-protocol-violation-on-invalid-op.md)). Closes the silent-drop class at src/dual_research/orchestrator/deep_research.py whose canonical instance — four ### RESOLVE blocks against items still in open at runs/20260526-102321-backend-language-choice/phase2/round-02-claude.md:230, :236, :242, and :248 (D-plan-c-02, D-plan-c-04, D-plan-c-05, Q-plan-c-01) — silently continue'd, leaving the reconstructed ledger to carry the four items as open indefinitely and burning three closeout rounds before the run died at phase2-r5-claude turn_inputs.

Sixteen new tests at tests/orchestrator/test_spec_0228_protocol_violation_emission.py — one per-site positive test for each of the six new emission sites (each asserts the violation_code, op_kind, expected_state, reason, from_state, and that the ledger item's state is unchanged); two carry-through tests confirming the pre-0228 raiser_self_address and terminal_state_re_address sites now populate the new fields; three "ent is None stays silent" tests pinning the identification-rule exclusion for the unknown-item path; and a replay test loading the dead-fixture round-02-claude.md verbatim that asserts exactly four resolve_from_non_addressed events fire against D-plan-c-02 / D-plan-c-04 / D-plan-c-05 / Q-plan-c-01, each carrying from_state="open" and expected_state="addressed".

Four further tests at tests/test_spec_0228_verifier_i4_4_gating.py lock in the severity flip: a parametrised assertion that the live verifier reports severity="gating" on I4.4 across all three anchor-run fixtures, a parametrised assertion that each fixture's frozen expected.json records severity: "gating", the CLI standalone-mode gate (no expected.json) on the dead fixture asserting rc == 1 with [gating] I4.4 and the four item IDs named in the rendered output, and a regression test that the baseline-included CLI invocation continues to return 0 (the spec 0225 contract — severity flip alone does not produce a baseline regression).

summary: Lifecycle-trace verifier — the 0114 unified contract in executable form (spec 0225).
items: Lifecycle-trace verifier — the 0114 unified contract in executable form ([spec 0225](specs/0225-lifecycle-trace-verifier.md)). Net-new dual-research verify ... CLI that audits any finished run against the 22 invariants from synthesis §3 (5 areas — phases, negotiations, categorisation, resolution lifecycle, liveness / terminal events).

The verifier IS the contract; before this spec the contract lived only as scattered prose across [spec 0114](specs/0114-unified-protocol-contract.md), [spec 0141](specs/0141-protocol-violation-guard.md), [spec 0214](specs/0214-phase4-draft-version-equality.md), and ../cowork/briefs/2026-05-26-logic-cutoff-synthesis.md.
With the verifier merged, contract drift surfaces in CI on the PR that introduces it rather than in a dead run a week later.

The 22 invariants are partitioned by severity: gating invariants whose failure fails CI today, and reporting invariants that log a delta without failing CI — each reporting invariant carries a documented promotion trigger (spec 0225 §5) so it tightens to gating once the underlying fix spec ships (I1.5 after the phase-4 budget contract lands, I2.4 after the addressee-obligation spec, I4.4 after the ProtocolViolation-emission spec).
I2.5 (self-report ⇄ ledger divergence) is reporting forever — synthesis §3 Area 2 is explicit that self-report is a cross-checked signal, never the source of truth.

New module src/dual_research/contract/verifier.py with verify_run(run_dir: Path) -> VerifierReport, VerifierReport.has_gating_failure, baseline_regressions(report, baseline), plus the _TurnFile op-block parser that diffs each turn .md file's ### RAISE / ### ADDRESS / ### RESOLVE / ### WITHDRAW / ### ACKNOWLEDGE blocks against the transcript's item_transitioned + protocol_violation events — the I4.4 silent-drop detector (a transcript-only scan cannot find Bug-A because the drop at deep_research.py:482 leaves no transcript event by design).

The verifier reuses the live contract substrate — imports ID_PATTERN from contract/ids.py, RAISABLE_IN + PHASE_TOKEN from contract/categories.py, the op-block regexes from contract/markers.py — so the assertion is that runs match the observed code's contract, never a re-spelled copy (synthesis §7.2).

I4.7 (capped-is-orchestrator-only) selects its predicate at module-load via dataclasses.fields(ItemTransitioned): primary event.via in {"hard_cap", "ghost_cap"} against the live ItemTransitioned.via field, build-time fallback to event.actor == "orchestrator" if via is renamed or removed.
The choice is recorded in verifier.I47_PREDICATE_NAME and surfaced in the JSON report.

New thin CLI driver src/dual_research/verifier_cli.py parses run-dir args + --json, looks for expected.json next to each run, computes per-invariant verdict diffs against the frozen baseline, exits non-zero on (a) any verdict diverging from baseline (regression or otherwise) or (b) any gating failure on a baseline-free run; the standalone "no baseline" mode falls back to "fail iff any gating fails." Three reference-run fixtures committed under tests/fixtures/anchor-runs/ — 20260521-010637-dvs-backend-language-choice (clean E2E, the live regression detector), 20260526-102321-backend-language-choice (today's primary failing run, gating I5.1 + I5.2 FAIL drives non-zero exit, reporting I4.4 logs the four dropped RESOLVE ops on D-plan-c-02 / D-plan-c-04 / D-plan-c-05 / Q-plan-c-01), 20260525-135006-backend-language-choice (second silent-death control isolating Bug B from Bug A).

Each fixture carries the verbatim transcript.jsonl + state.json + metrics.json + the phase0/ + phase2/ + phase4/ turn .md files (no phase1/ + phase3/ — no item events — no inputs/ + assembled-draft + searches/ audit bundles), plus a frozen expected.json capturing the LKG per-invariant verdict baseline; expected.json regeneration helper at tests.test_verifier.regenerate_baseline() for legitimate contract amendments.

New CI workflow .github/workflows/verifier-corpus.yml runs uv run dual-research verify tests/fixtures/anchor-runs/* on every PR and push to main; failure mode is verdict drift from any fixture's frozen baseline, including pass→fail regressions on reporting invariants per spec 0225 §2.5.

Fifty-seven new tests at tests/test_verifier.py — per-invariant positive + antipodal-absence pairs for all 22 invariants (I4.4 carries three cases per spec §6 — transition-match passes, ProtocolViolation-match passes, neither fails) plus three snapshot tests against the fixture corpus with targeted evidence assertions (the dead-run snapshot asserts that I4.4 cites all four named dropped items + I2.5 logs the round-3 and round-4 divergences).

Built on top of (not in scope to fix): reclassifying the offending bug-labeled specs 0137 / 0140 / 0218 / 0219 (deferred to a separate breaking-or-process spec per synthesis §6 action 5); closing the silent-drop at deep_research.py:482 via a ProtocolViolation emission spec (synthesis §6 action 3 — once that lands, I4.4 promotes from reporting to gating); the addressee-obligation enforcement in the orchestrator (synthesis §6 action 6 — once that lands, I2.4 promotes); the phase-4 budget contract (once that lands, I1.5 promotes); broader 31-run-corpus replay (this spec wires only the three named fixtures; nightly broader replay is a follow-up); the prompt-side investigation into why claude emits RESOLVE-from-open in the first place (synthesis §7.1 — separate authoring track).

summary: CLI registers SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT cancel handlers so the spec 0222 tombstone fires on raw signal kills (spec 0224).
items: CLI registers SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT cancel handlers so the spec 0222 tombstone fires on raw signal kills ([spec 0224](specs/0224-cli-signal-handlers-for-tombstone.md)). P1 silent-death contract gap: spec 0222 widened run_session's handler to except BaseException and added the _terminal_written finally-fallback, closing the in-process side of the Area-5 liveness invariant ("for every run_started, exactly one terminal event is emitted and metrics.ended_at is set").

But CPython's default disposition for SIGTERM and SIGHUP is immediate process termination without raising any exception — neither signal flows through Python's exception machinery, so the orchestrator's bare asyncio.run(...) entries at (_ingest) and (run_session) terminated the process before either the except BaseException block at or the finally-fallback at run.py:626 could run.
Run-20260526-102321 (mid-phase-2 silent death) is a likely instance of this failure.

Fix: introduce _run_with_signal_handlers(coro) in cli.py that calls loop.add_signal_handler(sig, main_task.cancel) for SIGTERM, SIGHUP, and SIGINT on the running event loop, awaits the inner coroutine, then removes the handlers in a finally: for test/loop hygiene.
Wraps both asyncio.run sites so ingest and orchestrator runs share the same protection — symmetric, no extra failure modes.
NotImplementedError (Windows) is swallowed; getattr(signal, name, None) guards the missing-SIGHUP-on-Windows case so import stays clean.
The orchestrator is mac-local-CLI today (the Fly app serves only the UI), so the POSIX-only API is acceptable as-is per spec 0224 §7.

Three regression tests at: each patches orch_run.run_phase0 to a long sleep, schedules os.kill(os.getpid(), ) after the run is in-flight, awaits cli._run_with_signal_handlers(orch_run.run_session(...)), and asserts (a) exactly one terminal event on disk, (b) it is run_failed or run_aborted, (c) metrics.ended_at is non-null.

The SIGINT test additionally asserts error_type=CancelledError (not the legacy KeyboardInterrupt) on the run_failed event — confirming the SIGINT UX swap from spec §3 ran, not the default CPython path.
All three tests fail against the pre-fix cli.py (AttributeError on the missing helper) and pass after the fix.

Out of scope per spec §7: sidecar watchdog / psutil-based external liveness monitor for SIGKILL / OOM-kill / hard-crash (impossible to handle in-process by design — kernel terminates without notification); changes to run.py:548's except BaseException or the _terminal_written fallback (spec 0222 implemented these correctly — this spec only routes new exception sources into them); Windows cross-platform support (deferred until the orchestrator targets Windows); reading Fly logs to confirm SIGTERM/SIGHUP caused run-20260526-102321 (Fly logs for that window are UI-only — the orchestrator was local).

summary: Phase 4 turn cards now render all four category Δ chips (Q→D→I→C) instead of only Q+D (spec 0223).
items: Phase 4 turn cards now render all four category Δ chips (Q→D→I→C) instead of only Q+D ([spec 0223](specs/0223-phase4-turn-cards-render-issues-comments-deltas.md)). Every per-turn card in the Phase 4 (Cross-review) section of the run-detail Timeline was missing its Issues (tone-err) and Comments (tone-idle) chips — only Questions (tone-info) and Disagreements (tone-warn) rendered.
The phase-header chip cluster correctly showed all four; per-turn cards silently violated the Q→D→I→C category-column alignment contract from design-system/SPEC.md §9.4 rule 8.
Root cause was a data-shape gap, not a render bug: attachItemStats in sets item.statsPhase on turn rows but never item.phase.
The chip-cluster ternary at reads item.phase ?? null, so null === 4 is false and every phase fell through to the two-category Q+D else branch.
Phase 2 worked by accident (it needs exactly Q+D); Phase 4 was silently truncated.
Single-line fix: add item.phase = phase next to the existing item.statsPhase = phase in attachItemStats.

The integer phase classification was already correct (Phase 0 via statsPhase === 0 at the push site; Phase 4 via String(index).startsWith('rev-'); Phase 2 as the default else); the fix just propagates it to the field consumers read.
Phase 0 and Phase 2 turn cards continue to render two chips (their else branch is unchanged); Phase 4 turn cards now render four.

The hypothesis-2 escape hatch from the spec (JSON-projection dropping zero-valued I/C keys) is dormant — TurnCategoryStats defaults all four CategoryCounters fields, so dataclasses.asdict always emits all four keys.

Two silent side-benefits: the run.violations lookup at run-detail.jsx:1165 and the findLedgerEntry call at run-detail.jsx:7717 — both of which read item.phase — now receive the actual integer instead of undefined.

Five source-pattern tests at per the SPEC.md §13 doctrine: positive for the four-category branch in run-detail.jsx, antipodal for phase === 4 paired with the two-category list (locks against revert), positive for the slim-Δ add={c.raised}/sub={c.closed} chip mapping, positive for item.phase = phase in live-data.jsx, and a structural assertion that the assignment lives inside the turn/turn-live branch of attachItemStats.
Cache-bust on live-data.jsx bumped to ?v=0223a in index.html.

Out of scope per spec §7: narrow-viewport overflow of the Phase 4 header chip cluster (deferred follow-up); broader phase === N audit (single-grep confirmed no immediate collateral; no consumer relied on item.phase being undefined).

summary: Orchestrator liveness tombstone: BaseException handler + finally-fallback + remove asymmetric stdout streaming (spec 0222).
items: Orchestrator liveness tombstone: BaseException handler + finally-fallback + remove asymmetric stdout streaming ([spec 0222](specs/0222-liveness-tombstone-baseexception-and-remove-stdout-streaming.md)). P0 silent-death bug that hid every other observability failure mode behind a missing terminal event.

Six runs since 2026-05-24 died with turn_inputs as their last transcript line — no run_failed, no run_aborted, no run_completed, metrics.ended_at = null — indistinguishable from "still running" to the dashboard, queue runner, and any reaper that tailed the transcript.

Establishes Area 5 of the unified contract (previously uncontracted): for every run_started, exactly one terminal event is emitted and metrics.ended_at is set — including on BaseException. Three coordinated code changes plus two regression tests. (1) Widened except to BaseException at.

Python's exception hierarchy splits at BaseException — asyncio.CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit are BaseException subclasses but not Exception subclasses, so the pre-fix except Exception let them escape the handler entirely; the finally: ran the push-watch drain but wrote no tombstone, and the process exited with the transcript unterminated.

Post-fix: catch BaseException, wrap metrics.mark_done() + metrics.save(...) and bus.publish(RunFailed(...)) in their own best-effort try/except BaseException blocks so a shutdown-time failure in either cannot suppress the load-bearing transcript.write("run_failed",...) tombstone, then re-raise KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit / asyncio.CancelledError so structured-concurrency cancellation propagates correctly and shells see the right exit code.

A new _terminal_written = False flag is initialised before the try: and set to True immediately after each terminal write (success path at run.py:521, except path after the new run_failed write); checked by the §4.3 fallback below. (2) Defensive finally-fallback tombstone at.
Order per §4.4: push-watch drain → metrics save → tombstone write, so the terminal event is included in the final hosted-UI push.

Runs only when _terminal_written == False (i.e. neither the success path nor the except path got far enough to write a terminal event — covers the partial-shutdown failure modes the except block alone cannot, e.g. a transcript.write that raises inside the except handler).

Both inner blocks are wrapped in try/except BaseException: pass so the fallback itself cannot raise; if metrics.save fails, the transcript still gets the run_aborted event (separate try), and if both fail the process exits unchanged from current behaviour — cannot regress.

The fallback writes event="run_aborted" with reason="terminal-event-fallback" so the audit trail distinguishes a happy-path-failed-twice abort from a normal run_failed. (3) Removed asymmetric stdout streaming at and.

Both call sites set stream_to=sys.stdout for claude turns only (openai turns set stream_to=None); the streaming was a foreground-debug convenience and is one of the plausible chains that turns a broken pipe into a BrokenPipeError inside an asyncio task whose cancellation cascade surfaces as asyncio.CancelledError at the orchestrator's top level.
Turn output is fully captured by the per-turn .md files and by the transcript event stream, so removing it loses nothing observable — and brings claude in line with openai (already stream_to=None).
Now-unused import sys removed from dr_run.py.

Two regression-prevention tests at: (1) a kill-test that raises asyncio.CancelledError mid-phase via a mocked run_phase0 and asserts the transcript carries exactly one terminal event (run_failed or run_aborted), metrics.ended_at is non-null, and the CancelledError propagates out of run_session; (2) a corrupt-transcript-handle test that patches Transcript.write to raise on run_completed / run_failed and asserts the finally: fallback still writes run_aborted with the documented reason and sets metrics.ended_at.
Both tests fail against the pre-fix except Exception code and pass after the fix.

Out of scope per spec §7: external reaper for SIGKILL / OOM (depends on Fly exit log read, deferred); ProtocolViolation on dropped state-machine ops at deep_research.py:482 (synthesis action 3); spec reclassification (0137 / 0140 / 0218 / 0219) + CLAUDE.md "contract-changing specs are not bugs" process rule; lifecycle-trace verifier; addressee-obligation feature spec; via_self_report convergence path (already at the four-via_* partition).

summary: DocumentModal body tab labeled "Output" instead of "Content" for doc / doc-live items (spec 0221).
items: DocumentModal body tab labeled "Output" instead of "Content" for doc / doc-live items ([spec 0221](specs/0221-doc-modal-output-label.md)). The Phase 3 converged-draft and Phase 5 final-draft full-view modals at previously rendered the body tab with the generic label: 'Content', which readers misread as prompt/spec content — missing that the actual phase output (the converged or final draft markdown) was sitting one tab away from "Agent Input".
Fix: introduce const isDocItem = item.kind === 'doc' || item.kind === 'doc-live' and gate the body tab's label as isDocItem ? 'Output': 'Content'.
The tab id stays 'content' so TABS_CANON ordering at continues to position the body tab second on Phase 3 (after "Agent Input") and as the only tab on Phase 5 (no turnKey → no input tab).
turn / turn-live / plan / plan-live modals route through NegotiateReviewModal / DraftReviewModal and are untouched.
Three source-pattern tests at lock the post-fix shape (positive ternary + predicate definition) plus antipodal-absence of the pre-fix unconditional label: 'Content' block, per the spec 0206 doctrine.

summary: Fixed: Changelog side-menu version-num column overlapped 6-character…
items: Changelog side-menu version-num column overlapped 6-character versions ([spec 0220.1](specs/0220.1-side-menu-version-num-collision-long-versions.md)). .hiw-overlay__menu-list.menu-section-num at was width: 18px — fits the legacy hand-curated 3-character versions (0.5, 1.0) but not the 6-character 1.45.0 shape that now dominates the auto-generated list after spec 0220.
Result: the trailing .0 of the version visually overlapped the summary, producing strings like 1.45In-app Changelog auto-generate.
CSS-only fix: width: 18px → min-width: 48px; margin-right: var(--s-2);.
min-width (not width) keeps overflow graceful — a 7-character version like 100.0.0 will push the column wider, not collide.
The rule lands in both AND (the DS file previously had no .menu-section-num rule — this commit closes that DS-sync gap as a bonus).
Side effect by design: the How-it-works tab's section numbers (1, 2, …) now sit in the same 48px column — visually aligns the two tabs that share the menu rail.

summary: In-app Changelog auto-generated from CHANGELOG.md (spec 0220).
items: In-app Changelog auto-generated from CHANGELOG.md ([spec 0220](specs/0220-in-app-changelog-auto-generated.md)). The Changelog tab at /#how-it-works was 33 releases behind (last hand-curated entry v1.35.0; current shipped v1.44.25) because the renderer read from a VERSION_NOTES JS literal that no PR had appended to since spec 0175.
Six coordinated changes close the gap. (1) New build-time generator at scripts/build_version_notes.py parses CHANGELOG.md into newest-first JSON at src/dual_research/ui/static/version-notes.json.

Regex-only prettify pass strips path-shape markdown link wrappers (` → dropped entirely), preserves spec NNNN verbatim, converts bold/backticks to /, sentence-splits bullets > 240 chars, and reshapes Previously X; now Y into Now/Was anatomy.

The empty-paren cleanup uses (?<=\s)\(\s*[,;]?\s*\) so legitimate foo() call sites in blocks survive. (2) Per-version overrides at src/dual_research/ui/static/version-notes-overrides.json are the escape hatch — full-record replace, no field-level merge.

Seeded verbatim from the historical hand-curated VERSION_NOTES (v1.2.0–v1.35.0, 39 entries) so today's prose isn't regressed by the prettifier. (3) User-facing classifier (regex-only): an entry is user_facing: false if its cited spec's body contains zero references under src/dual_research/ui/static/ or design-system/.

The narrow heuristic (matches the spec's intent statement "Specs that ARE the application UI surface") filters orchestrator/protocol-only fixes out of the default view; the per-version override carries an optional user_facing field for edge cases. (4) ChangelogList rewired to fetch the JSON sidecar on mount via a module-level useVersionNotes() hook (shared with HowItWorksBody's side menu so the same fetch services both surfaces).

Hash routing for #how-it-works#cl- anchors marks the matching ChangelogEntry with a new forceOpen prop that overrides CollapsibleSection's defaultOpen AND any persisted localStorage collapse state on initial render — subsequent toggles persist normally.

A new [Internal N] filter chip (tone neutral, default OFF) toggles internal entries; when ON they render as flat .changelog-internal-row one-liners (vX.Y.Z · date · Internal — · spec chips · bump chip) interleaved chronologically with ChangelogEntry cards.

CSS lands in both src/dual_research/ui/static/components.css AND design-system/assets/styles/composed-components.css per the CLAUDE.md two-file CSS sync rule. (5) AppVersionChip rewired from inert
to a

The pre-fix comment claiming "Click → how-it-works page" was a lie; spec 0220 makes it true. (6) /dev-next step 15b now invokes uv run python scripts/build_version_notes.py immediately after CHANGELOG.md is written, regenerating the sidecar in the same PR commit; a CI guard (--check mode) fails the build if the on-disk JSON drifts behind.
CONTRIBUTING.md §5 updated to describe the auto-generation flow (the old "append to VERSION_NOTES" bullet is gone).

Twenty-nine new tests at tests/test_spec_0220_in_app_changelog.py cover source-pattern anatomy across all six surfaces (positive + antipodal-absence pairs per spec 0206) plus generator-unit coverage of the prettifier branches, bump inference, spec-ID extraction (composite IDs like 0211.3), classification (UI ref / DS ref / missing-spec defaults), idempotence, and the CI sidecar-sync guard.
