summary: Fixed: Phase-4 §3.2 section-delta drafter contract —…
items: Phase-4 §3.2 section-delta drafter contract — reviewer/validator collision, heading-mismatch corruption, REPLACE_SECTION budget overrun, mid-phase resume waste ([spec 0219](specs/0219-phase4-section-delta-contract-v2.md)): six coordinated changes attack the four bugs that made spec 0218 a net regression on the backend-language-choice smoking-gun run (runs/20260526-000758-backend-language-choice/ — 6× revised_draft_delta_violation, 3× repair_invoked, terminal run_failed exit 52, draft-v2.md ballooned to ~90KB of duplicated content). (1) Reviewer template drops ## Revised draft: review_round_n_prompt_v2 now computes a role-conditional doctrine block — drafter sees the section-delta op grammar plus the literal current-draft heading list (§3.3 below); reviewer sees a one-line _REVIEWER_REVISION_NOTE instructing them to OMIT the section entirely.

The smoking-gun was the reviewer dutifully writing "(reviewer — no draft edits)" inside ## Revised draft and the role-blind validator rejecting it every round, exhausting the repair budget. (2) _assert_v2_well_formed_turn gates on is_drafter: the §3.2 delta-op check now only fires for the phase-4 drafter; reviewer turns with a missing, empty, or placeholder ## Revised draft body never trip the gate.

parse_v2_with_repair accepts is_drafter: bool + prior_draft: str | None and threads both through the validator so heading-mismatch / anchor-mismatch / missing-reason: errors route through the same one-shot repair plumbing. (3) Literal current-draft headings injected into the drafter prompt (— extract_draft_headings; — _drafter_revision_doctrine_v2; wired at ): the drafter sees the literal ## heading list parsed from current_draft_path so every delta op targets a real heading rather than drifting to brief-criteria numbering (2.1 — Executive Summary… against draft headings 1.

Summary, 2. Findings, …). (4) apply_revised_draft_deltas hard-fails on unknown REPLACE_SECTION / EDIT_SECTION heading: mismatched headings raise ProtocolParseError("replace_section_unknown_heading" / "edit_section_unknown_heading",...) with the valid-headings list, replacing the spec 0218 silent APPEND promotion that corrupted draft-v2.md.

Errors route through the existing repair flow. (5) New ### EDIT_SECTION surgical op (— EditSectionOp + _parse_edit_section_pairs): ANCHOR: / REPLACE_WITH: pairs (multiple per block, applied in document order) let the drafter target a 5-line typo fix in ~100 output tokens vs ~2000 with REPLACE_SECTION.
Byte-exact anchor matching; 0 matches raises edit_section_anchor_not_found, >1 matches raises edit_section_anchor_ambiguous.

Doctrine update in the drafter prompt: default to EDIT_SECTION; use REPLACE_SECTION only when rewriting >50% of a section AND include a leading reason: line (validator-enforced — missing reason raises replace_section_missing_reason); REPLACE_DRAFT_FULL remains the escape hatch.

Attacks the 16,758-token-busts-cap symptom by shrinking per-op payloads without raising _TURN_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS further. (6) Phase-4 round counter checkpointed per round: new SessionState.phase4_round: int = 0 field is persisted after each phase-4 round completes; _drive_interaction_phase seeds round_no from it on phase-4 entry so a resumed run picks up at round N+1 instead of restarting at round 1 (~$1.40 per resume per agent on prod-tier models saved).
Reset to 0 on the phase-3→phase-4 transition.
Backwards compatible — legacy state files without the field deserialise to 0.

Twelve regression tests at cover each bug: reviewer-with/without-Revised-draft passes the validator, drafter-with-empty-or-prose Revised draft still fails (gate doesn't accidentally pass drafter violations), REPLACE_SECTION on unknown heading raises with valid-headings list, EDIT_SECTION ANCHOR/REPLACE_WITH roundtrip + not-found + ambiguous, REPLACE_SECTION missing reason hard-fails, phase4_round round-trips + resume seeds correctly, and an end-to-end replay of the vendored smoking-gun fixture at confirming the 8 mismatched REPLACE_SECTION ops now raise replace_section_unknown_heading cleanly rather than corrupting the draft via APPEND promotion.
The 0218 test fixture at gains a reason: line on its REPLACE_SECTION to honour the new contract.

summary: Phase-4 drafter truncation no longer destroys STATUS (spec 0218): four coordinated changes make phase-4 STATUS-block survival structural rather than aspirational.
items: Phase-4 drafter truncation no longer destroys STATUS ([spec 0218](specs/0218-phase4-status-survives-truncation.md)): four coordinated changes make phase-4 STATUS-block survival structural rather than aspirational. (1) STATUS-first ordering — the ## Status block now sits immediately after ## Stance in every negotiation / review prompt (phase 0 round 1, phase 0 round N, phase 2 round 1, phase 2 round N, phase 4 round 1, phase 4 round N) in.

STATUS is the smallest section in the response (≤ 200 tokens for the action arrays + counters) and the only one whose contents are irrecoverable from priors; placing it at the top of the response means it always lands even when the ## Revised draft body that follows runs past the output-token budget.

A new _STATUS_FIRST_ORDERING_CALLOUT constant explains the rationale inline above the section list. (2) Section-delta drafter contract — the drafter's ## Revised draft body is now a sequence of ### REPLACE_SECTION / ### APPEND_SECTION / ### DELETE_SECTION operation blocks, with ### REPLACE_DRAFT_FULL as the escape hatch for structural rewrites.

Parser surface adds extract_revised_draft_deltas + apply_revised_draft_deltas at returning a RevisedDraftDeltas | RevisedDraftFull discriminated union; the dr_run.py drafter-revision callback dispatches on the union variant against the prior draft-vN.md.

Legacy full-prose ## Revised draft bodies (no ### REPLACE_* / ### APPEND_* / ### DELETE_* / ### REPLACE_DRAFT_FULL sub-heading) raise ProtocolParseError("revised_draft_body_missing_delta_op") and route through repair.

Mismatched-heading REPLACE_SECTION promotes to APPEND_SECTION with a logged protocol-violation; same-heading double REPLACE_SECTION applies last-writer-wins with a logged violation. (3) parse_with_repair wired into dr_run.py — a new parse_v2_with_repair sibling at runs validator + one-shot repair between run_one_call and the canonical write.
_assert_v2_well_formed_turn rejects turns whose ## Status block is missing (the headline failure mode) and turns whose ## Revised draft body lacks delta-op sub-headings.

finish_reason in {"max_tokens", "length"} is treated as a synthetic parse failure regardless of body shape — a truncated turn whose tail bytes coincidentally look STATUS-valid is still untrustworthy and routes through repair.
Truncated text is saved to .malformed-.md for audit; the canonical path is only written after the repaired turn parses clean.

RepairTracker semantics unchanged — one-shot budget per agent per phase, exit 52 on second consecutive failure. (4) Output-budget bump + Anthropic beta header — _TURN_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 16384 in (up from 8192), and the output-128k-2025-02-19 beta header is added alongside the existing extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11 beta in so the request budget actually exceeds Claude's 8K default cap.
Defense-in-depth for ### REPLACE_DRAFT_FULL and large single-section rewrites; the typical section-delta round still emits ~2–4K tokens.

Eleven regression tests at lock the STATUS-first ordering across all 5 prompt sites, section-delta application semantics, the prose-body rejection, both max_tokens + length truncation paths, the truncated-turn-never-lands-canonical contract end-to-end, and the regression-replay rejection of the captured phase-4 R2-claude turn shape from runs/20260525-162909-backend-language-choice/.

summary: Fixed: STATUS action arrays in interaction-phase prompts…
items: STATUS action arrays in interaction-phase prompts now declare a canonical-ID-only contract ([spec 0217.1](specs/0217.1-openai-status-raised-canonical-ids.md)): the STATUS-footer placeholders in used permissive phrasing (RAISED_THIS_TURN: [list of IDs the orchestrator will assign] for round-1 footers, and the bare RAISED_THIS_TURN: [...] ellipsis everywhere else), which let agents substitute descriptive prose for canonical IDs.

The smoking-gun case is openai's round-1 STATUS array in the 20260525-135006-backend-language-choice session — captured verbatim at — where the array carried multi-line description strings ("disagreement: Go #1 vs C# #1", …) instead of D-plan-g-01-style IDs.
Spec 0217's STATUS-pass at parses canonical IDs and silently drops non-ID entries (per §8's spurious-ID mitigation), so the openai-side negotiation never reached the reconstructed ledger.

Fix: (1) tighten every placeholder in the inline round-1 footers (phase 0 / phase 2 / phase 4) plus the shared _status_footer_for_phase helper to [,...]; (2) add a centralised callout constant (_STATUS_ARRAY_CONTRACT_CALLOUT + a round-1 variant that explains the orchestrator assigns IDs from ### RAISE blocks) that prints inline above every ## Status block in the four round-1/round-N interaction prompts (phase 2 + phase 4).
The reconstructor is unchanged — the fix lives at the protocol-contract layer per spec 0217's handoff §3.4 ("path (a) is the structurally correct fix — STATUS arrays should be ID-only by contract").
Three new tests at pin the post-fix shape (substring IDs only present) and the antipodal absence of the pre-fix placeholders.

Existing spec-0217 suite continues to pass unchanged — the round-01-openai descriptive-string fixture stays as-is and continues to be silently dropped, but new sessions will produce canonical IDs naturally once agents read the tightened contract.

summary: Fixed: Phase-2 / phase-4 ledger reconstructors now…
items: Phase-2 / phase-4 ledger reconstructors now honor STATUS.RESOLVED_THIS_TURN / WITHDRAWN_THIS_TURN ([spec 0217](specs/0217-ledger-status-block-authoritative-for-closures.md)): the per-kind reconstructors at and used to recognise closures only via section-tail scanning (## Resolved or non-blocking differences or per-item D-N: label — status: resolved).

When agents started ratifying via the ## Ratifying my own items / ### RESOLVE D-N block shape, closures became invisible to the ledger even though the agents' STATUS.RESOLVED_THIS_TURN: [...] arrays were correct.
Phase 2 then ran three extra administrative-closeout rounds (20260525-135006-backend-language-choice burned ~2h vs. the spec'd 20–30 min).

Both reconstructors now run a STATUS pass per turn: RESOLVED_THIS_TURN / WITHDRAWN_THIS_TURN are the canonical closure channel; section-tail scanning stays as a legacy fallback; STATUS wins on conflict.
By symmetry, RAISED_THIS_TURN seeds minimal entries when the legacy body-section parser produced none (necessary for the new ### RAISE block protocol where item IDs only appear in STATUS).

Composite IDs (D-plan-c-01, Q-plan-c-02) match through a canonical-form helper that zero-pads numeric tails and lowercases composite tails; the spurious-ID mitigation (§8) drops STATUS-listed IDs that were never raised in any prior round.
### RESOLVE D-N blocks are explicitly NOT parsed (§3.4 — STATUS stays the canonical channel; no third parsing grammar).
Phase-4 coverage is automatic — build_phase_ledger at reuses the same reconstructors.

Seven new tests at cover STATUS-only closure / legacy-section-tail / STATUS-wins-on-conflict for both reconstructors plus a hermetic replay against rounds 1–3 of the smoking-gun session (fixture under tests/fixtures/spec_0217/) — locks in that all 5 D-items (D-plan-c-01..05) and 2 Q-items (Q-plan-c-01..02) close by round 3, not at the round-5 hard cap.

summary: Fixed: Silent raiser self-ADDRESS drop now emits…
items: Silent raiser self-ADDRESS drop now emits ProtocolViolation ([spec 0216](specs/0216-raiser-self-address-observability.md)): when an agent ADDRESSes an item it itself raised (protocol-forbidden — only the other agent's items can be addressed), the orchestrator was silently dropping the block at with no event emitted, leaving the misuse invisible to the dashboard and transcript.

Now emits ProtocolViolation(violation_code="raiser_self_address", item_id=…, from_state=…) while preserving the existing drop semantics (the item's state is unchanged — same continue, same downstream behaviour).
Field shape mirrors the peer terminal_state_re_address violation a few lines below.

The Ratifying-section instructions for all three interaction phases (0/2/4) at gained an explicit "Do NOT use ADDRESS here; ADDRESS is reserved for the other agent's items" clarification — additive text inside the existing parenthesised instruction blocks, no structural-marker change.
Doc-comment on ProtocolViolation in updated to enumerate both codes in use today (terminal_state_re_address + the new raiser_self_address).

New regression tests at cover the violation-emission paths for open and addressed source states, a replay test against the actual failing turn from the 20260521-010637-dvs-backend-language-choice run (fixture committed under tests/fixtures/raiser_self_address_replay/), and two negatives that lock the gate didn't widen (other-agent ADDRESS still transitions normally; raiser RESOLVE/WITHDRAW still ratifies clean).

summary: Fixed: In-round partner blindness in list_turns (spec…
items: In-round partner blindness in list_turns ([spec 0215](specs/0215-fix-in-round-partner-blindness.md)): every interaction phase (0, 2, 4) runs agents sequentially within a round, but list_turns(up_to_round=N) was dropping both agents' round-N files via a strict r >= up_to_round filter at.

The second-to-execute agent never saw its partner's freshly-written turn until the *next* round, silently delaying convergence by one full round in every phase — observed in the local 20260521-010637-dvs-backend-language-choice run where OpenAI cited an open blocker that Claude had RESOLVED on disk milliseconds before.

summary: Phase 4 hash-gate deadlock (spec 0214): the cross-review convergence gate no longer asks each agent to compute a SHA-256 hash of the draft body.
items: Phase 4 hash-gate deadlock ([spec 0214](specs/0214-drop-phase4-agent-emitted-hash-gate.md)): the cross-review convergence gate no longer asks each agent to compute a SHA-256 hash of the draft body.

The pre-fix gate at _phase4_artifact_hash_match in required both agents to emit byte-identical SHA-256 digests of the draft text — a hash an LLM cannot reliably reproduce because the orchestrator's canonical_hash applies smart-quote folding + whitespace collapsing before hashing.
Either side would fabricate a digest or refuse on principle, the hashes never matched, and Phase 4 ran to the hard cap.

Convergence now requires both agents to emit STATUS: AGREED with matching draft_version pointers anchored against ctx.state.draft_round via the lifted phase4_version_gate(parsed_a, parsed_b, *, ctx_draft_round) helper, and the orchestrator computes the canonical draft hash itself via the new _compute_draft_sha_if_present(ctx) helper, recording it on the new Phase4Complete.draft_file_sha256 field for provenance.

The same-round revise-then-AGREE failure mode (drafter bumps to v and emits AGREED in the same turn before the orchestrator advances the pointer) is rejected by the ver_a == ver_b == ctx_draft_round cross-check.
The spec-0137/0140 escape valve (via_artifact_promotion) is preserved as a dead-letter safety net.

items: Spec 0201 — Branch & safety hygiene: verified deletes, dirty-tree refusal, pre-push branch assertion ([spec 0201](specs/0201-branch-and-safety-hygiene-verified-deletes-dirty-tree-refusal-pre-push-assertion.md)).
Refactoring: success-path orchestrator behavior unchanged; only failure-path behavior tightens.

Three independent safety nets land in /dev-next (and one inherited gate in /dev-queue-run) plus a backstop sweeper in this repo. (1) Verified branch delete after merge — ~/.claude/skills/dev-next/SKILL.md step 19 gains a post-gh pr merge --delete-branch verification block that asserts git ls-remote --heads origin spec/${SPEC_ID}-${SLUG} and git branch --list... are both empty; one explicit retry via git push origin --delete + git branch -D, then halt with status: merged (not flipped to deployed).

Branch-ID grammar accepts both integer and decimal IDs per spec 0199 (NNNN or NNNN.M interpolated as opaque strings). (2) Dirty-tree refusal at pre-flight — ~/.claude/skills/dev-next/SKILL.md step 2 and ~/.claude/skills/dev-queue-run/SKILL.md step 2 hard-halt on non-empty git status --porcelain, surface the file list verbatim, and offer exactly two recovery paths: git stash push -u -m "..." (preferred, reversible) or an explicit named-files-with-commit-message instruction.
Ambiguous phrases ("run it", "go ahead", "do it", "run it as-is") are not commit license; the orchestrator must not synthesize a "queue reshuffle" commit.

Canonical counter-example called out inline: the 2026-05-22 incident (commit 933673d, reverted b0ae421) that dropped spec 0177 and demoted 0176 back to draft. (3) Pre-push branch-identity assertion — ~/.claude/skills/dev-next/SKILL.md steps 17, 18, and 15-CP each gain a hard-halt assertion comparing git branch --show-current against spec/${SPEC_ID}-${SLUG} before any feature-branch push.
Halt is hard, no warning, no retry.
Scope: feature-branch pushes only (post-merge git push origin main is governed by its explicit refspec and stays unguarded).

Protects against resume-mode silent-checkout-failure leaking spec-targeted commits onto main. (4) Backstop sweeper — new scripts/sweep_stale_branches.sh lists spec/* on origin, queries each PR's state via gh pr view --json state,mergedAt, deletes only when state == "MERGED", and reports OPEN/CLOSED-not-merged/no-PR branches contributing to a non-zero exit code.
Idempotent; modeled on scripts/sweep_stale_blues.sh.
Per-cycle verified delete in §2.1 is the primary mechanism; the sweeper covers historical drift and rare races surviving the verified retry.

Acceptance dry-runs: sweeper against current origin returns "no stale spec/* branches on origin" exit 0 (baseline clean); branch-identity assertion fires correctly on a mismatch (spec/0201-foo expected, spec/0201-branch-and-safety-hygiene-... actual) and passes silently on a match.

summary: Spec 0200 — Fly deploy simplification: drop bluegreen, no-retry-on-failure rule, codify recovery path (spec 0200).
items: Spec 0200 — Fly deploy simplification: drop bluegreen, no-retry-on-failure rule, codify recovery path ([spec 0200](specs/0200-fly-deploy-simplification-drop-bluegreen-no-retry-rule-codify-recovery.md)).
Refactoring: internal deploy mechanics only, no user-facing change.
fly.toml switches from strategy = "bluegreen" to strategy = "rolling" at fly.toml:21.

Bluegreen (spec 0159) reduced cold-boot timeouts but exposed a worse mode: the destroy-lease on the old "blue" cohort races with parallel flyctl sessions, leaving zombie machines that accumulate across deploys (handoffs 0187/0188/0189, project_fly_lease_drift_recovery).
Rolling replaces machines one at a time in place with no parallel cohort and no destroy-cohort lease, structurally eliminating the race rather than patching around it.

The 90s health-check grace (fly.toml:49) — calibrated in spec 0159 for shared-cpu-1x:512MB cold-boots — and min_machines_running = 1 together cover the cold-boot regression risk; capacity stays at ≥ 1 through the rollout.
Single-machine immediate was considered and rejected (would introduce ~30s downtime per deploy and remove HA).

/dev-next step 21 (out-of-band, in ~/.claude/skills/dev-next/SKILL.md) gains a five-case decision matrix for non-zero fly deploy exits: run fly status first; route to case 1 (all new, all healthy — deploy actually succeeded, only cleanup failed; sweep + proceed), case 2 (mixed but all healthy — sweep + proceed), case 3 (only old version present — genuine failure, mark status: failed, failure_step: deploy, halt), case 4 (mixed but new unhealthy — same halt branch as case 3), or case 5 (fly status itself errors — halt with the original deploy error).
Hard rule: the orchestrator NEVER calls fly deploy more than once within one /dev-next invocation — the two-shots-in-one-cycle behavior that amplified the orphan count is eliminated by construction.
Skill step 21 also gains a pointer to project_fly_lease_drift_recovery.md as the incident-history narrative, with the matrix called out as its actionable distillation.

scripts/sweep_stale_blues.sh header comment updated to document its rolling-era role — the tag-based primary filter routinely finds zero candidates on healthy rolling clusters; the spec-0193 image-based fallback becomes the primary recovery mechanism.
The script's runtime behavior is unchanged — the four-gate safety cascade already protects against zeroing the cluster mid-rollout.
No code change to the sweep script itself.

items: Spec 0193 — image-based fallback filter for scripts/sweep_stale_blues.sh ([spec 0193](specs/0193-stale-blue-sweep-image-based-filter.md)).
Spec 0162 added the safe_to_destroy-tag filter to clean up stale blues after a deploy.

Today's queue drain (specs 0187 → 0192) demonstrated a second failure mode on every single deploy: Fly leaves blues hanging WITHOUT the safe_to_destroy tag, so the tag filter prints no stale blues while the cluster is still oversize.
The fallback runs only when the tag filter found 0 candidates AND the cluster exceeds --expected-count.
New get_current_release_image() helper queries fly releases --app … --json for the latest status: "complete" release's image_ref (or reads a sibling .release.json fixture in test mode).

When gate 4 fails (no green present), the fallback refuses, dumps metadata for triage, exits 0.

The original spec-0162 tag filter is unchanged and runs first; the fallback is strictly additive. 6 new tests in tests/spec0193/ (5 fixture-based scenarios + 1 invariant — script always exits 0) drive the script as a subprocess with --input fixtures.

items: Fixed. Spec 0174 — /api/data subrequest-limit blowup (502) + dashboard poll dropped to 5s ([spec 0174](specs/0174-fix-api-data-subrequest-blowup-and-5s-poll.md)).
The Cloudflare Pages Function at was making 1 REST tree call + N per-file REST blob calls (~162 at today's repo size).
Cloudflare's free-tier subrequest cap is 50, so the Function blew the cap and returned 502 — Too many subrequests by single Worker invocation on every request.
The dashboard at the live URL fell back to the build-time-baked content and never refreshed.

Changed. GitHub blob fetching uses GraphQL — functions/api/data.js now POSTs a single batched GraphQL query that asks for Repository.object(expression: ":") as aliased fields for every file the tree walk discovered.
Net subrequest count drops from 1 + N (~162) to ~2 (1 tree REST call + 1 GraphQL POST).
At repos > 400 files, batches in chunks of 400 fields per POST — still ~3 subrequests max at 1000-spec scale.
The existing 15s edge-cache + stale-while-revalidate=60s headers stay. (functions/api/data.js:170–211)
Dashboard poll interval: 15s → 5s (DASHBOARD_BOOTSTRAP_JS).
With the GraphQL fix the Function returns in ~300–500 ms, and the response is edge-cached for 15s, so most polls hit Cloudflare's edge cache rather than reaching GitHub.
Perceived end-to-end latency from origin/main change → dashboard repaint drops from ~15s to ~5–7s.
— fixtures rewritten to mock the GraphQL POST.

New regression-prevention assertion: the happy-path test asserts fetchMock.mock.calls.length === 2 (1 tree + 1 GraphQL), so any future regression that reintroduces per-file fetches blows the count and trips the test.
New test added for the GraphQL errors path → 502.

(1) Active-agent badges now pulse. The two .as.in-header AgentStrip badges in the Timeline pane (Claude in .tl__head, GPT in .tl__tabs, placed by spec 0133) previously signalled "this model is doing work" only through a 6 px dot in their right cluster — easy to miss in a crowded pane.

A five-variant prototype study at prototypes/active-agent-pulse/mockup.html (soft halo, gradient sweep, elevation breathing, border-tint glow, combined) converged on Variant B — a gentle agent-tinted soft-light gradient that sweeps right-to-left across the badge surface over 3.2 s. 18% alpha against the surface-container background; the sweep is felt before it's seen and never competes with the inner dot pulse.
Both agents can be live simultaneously; the GPT badge carries animation-delay: -1.6s so they don't lock-step.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the live state degrades to a static surface-container-high tint so liveness stays legible without motion.
New --agent-{a,b}-rgb triples in tokens.css carry the alpha-friendly palette.

(2) Critique card height parity. Every critique-pane QuestionThread previously rendered a small "id: D-plan-c-01" line under the chip header — always present, even when collapsed — which combined with the parent .qthread's gap: 12px added ~28 px to every card relative to the matching timeline turn card.

The id was fully redundant (the D/Q/I/C prefix duplicates the category chip, the -c-/-g- suffix duplicates the provider icon chip, the round counter duplicates the "raised in r{N}" chip; the phase fragment is disambiguated by the surrounding .crit-group header).
Dropping the line lets every collapsed critique card match the vertical footprint of a collapsed timeline turn card.
The expanded card's gap behaviour (header → lifecycle body separator) is unchanged.
(3) Run-id chip in RunDetailHeader row 2. Adds a RunIDChip rendering the full run.id to the right-side cluster of PhaseDotsRow, immediately left of the started / elapsed / round metadata.
Click copies the id to the clipboard; the chip's title swaps to "copied!" for 1.4 s as confirmation.
Uses the existing .rid chip primitive — no new design-system surface.
The 4-char hex prefix in the run-list page is unchanged; this is an additional affordance for referring to the run elsewhere.

summary: Spec 0137 — Substantive-convergence escape valve for hash-drift dead-loops (spec 0137).
items: Spec 0137 — Substantive-convergence escape valve for hash-drift dead-loops ([spec 0137](specs/0137-substantive-convergence-escape-valve.md)).

Production run 81cc (20260520-170146-dvs-backend-language-choice) reproduced an issue the user has been chasing since the legacy → Deep Research cutover: in Phase 2, by round 5 every ledger item was terminal (12 questions / disagreements all resolved or withdrawn), in rounds 6 / 7 / 8 both agents emitted STATUS: AGREED with matching DRAFTER: claude, and no new items were raised — but the phase exited at hard cap with converged=false drafter=null.

Three rounds of LLM spend (~$1.50, 70+ seconds per round) produced zero substantive content; the agents kept paraphrasing their own AGREED_PLAN bodies (claude's ~19 k normalised chars, openai's ~14 k, hashes thrashing round-over-round) and never landed byte-identical text.
The same shape was observable in Phase 0 round 4.

Root cause. The Deep Research three-gate convergence check (orchestrator/closeout.py::check_convergence) requires (i) both STATUS: AGREED, (ii) zero non-terminal items, AND (iii) byte-equal artifact hashes.

The legacy phase2.py carried a Spec 0032 hash-drift escape valve (force-verbatim repair turn → canonical-promote on second drift) for exactly this case; the Spec 0114 cutover to dr_run.py::_drive_interaction_phase did not port it.

The closeout mechanism handles "both AGREED + items non-terminal", hard-cap handles "ran out of rounds", but the "both AGREED + items terminal + hash drift" gap had no handler — the agents iterated until hard cap doing nothing.

summary: Spec 0136 follow-up — Supabase list path + non-zero exit-code generalisation.
items: Spec 0136 follow-up — Supabase list path + non-zero exit-code generalisation. The v1.8.1 spec-0136 fix unified the status truth table for the disk-backed paths (summarize_run + load_run_snapshot) and verified locally that DVS-backend / pv-backend-language / LLM-vs-human-grading all flipped from running/completed → deadlocked.

But the user immediately surfaced the same divergence on the hosted surface — and rightly so: there was a third status deriver, _status_from_columns in server.py:1075, that maps the Supabase runs table columns onto the UI status enum for the All-Runs list when the server runs in Supabase mode.

That helper called derive_run_status but flattened exit_code into derived run_failed / hard_cap_hit booleans before the truth table saw it, which discarded the exit_code == 0 + not-done signal and left the hosted list reading running indefinitely for any pushed run that exited cleanly without reaching done — exactly the DVS-backend / LLM-vs-human-grading pattern.
The detail-page path on hosted was correct (it materialises the session through load_run_snapshot, which already had the fix); only the list path was wrong.

summary: Spec 0136 — Unify run-status derivation across the All-Runs list, the run-detail page, and the orchestrator's exit-code emission (spec 0136).
items: Spec 0136 — Unify run-status derivation across the All-Runs list, the run-detail page, and the orchestrator's exit-code emission ([spec 0136](specs/0136-unify-run-status-derivation.md)).

Two independent live runs surfaced the same symptom on the same day: All-Runs list said running while the run-detail page said completed, even though the run had silently exited at the Phase 2 hard cap without converging.
Truthfully it was deadlocked, but neither surface said so.
The detail-page timeline also dropped the last round's output card — a downstream symptom of the wrong terminal status.

Three layered bugs: (1) the orchestrator's shared _drive_interaction_phase driver gated HardCapHit emission on hard_cap_remaining_items being non-empty, so the "every item terminal but no AGREED status" pattern silently exited with exit_code 0; (2) the All-Runs path's _scan_terminal_signals didn't read run_completed at all, so its derive_run_status fall-through swallowed any "exited cleanly without reaching done" case as running forever; (3) the run-detail path's _on_run_completed mapped exit_code 0 → "completed" blindly without cross-checking state.phase or final_emitted_to.
Three coordinated changes.

summary: Spec 0135 — Phase 0 round cards + side-by-side critique modal (spec 0135).
items: Spec 0135 — Phase 0 round cards + side-by-side critique modal ([spec 0135](specs/0135-phase0-round-cards-and-side-by-side-critique.md)).

Spec 0114 made Phase 0 a full multi-round brief negotiation under the Deep Research protocol — the same _drive_interaction_phase coroutine that drives Phase 2 (plan negotiation) and Phase 4 (draft review) — but nine downstream wiring gaps prevented the round-by-round surface from showing.

The timeline collapsed Phase 0 back into two single-shot "preflight" cards regardless of how many rounds the agents actually negotiated; the full-view modal opened a single-pane response viewer instead of the side-by-side critique pane used everywhere else; review items, ledgers, summaries, token usage, and live-streaming bodies were all gated to phases 2 and 4.
This spec closes every gap with surgical, structurally-mirrored changes — no protocol churn, no new prompts, no new on-disk artefacts.

summary: Spec 0133 follow-up — bump narrow-mode breakpoint 1499 → 1799 px.
items: Spec 0133 follow-up — bump narrow-mode breakpoint 1499 → 1799 px. Post-deploy validation surfaced that the spec-0133 narrow-mode rules weren't kicking in for the most common laptop viewports.

The original breakpoint (max-width: 1499px) was inherited from SPEC-0125's filter-row rule, but the spec-0133 block grew to govern much more (relocated agent pills + Bar 1 compaction + Bar 2 status/agent label collapse + segmented control icons-only).

The combined wide-mode content (Timeline pill + Conversation/Consumption tabs in one row; Critique title + three phase tabs + three counter triples in another; ten filter chips with full labels in a third) needs each two-pane column at ≥ ~900 px to fit, which requires viewport ≥ ~1800 px.
MacBook Pro 16" (1728 px), MacBook Pro 14" (1512 px), and the typical half-screen browser window on a 27" display all sit in the 1500–1799 range and were missing narrow rules entirely.
Bumping the shared block at components.css:763 from 1499 → 1799 px covers them.
The unrelated .agent-input (components.css:1072) and .resp-grid (components.css:2987) breakpoints stay at 1499 — different layouts, different threshold.

items: Added. Spec 0091 — Phase 4 drafter-engagement gate (close the round-1 sycophantic-APPROVED loophole) ([spec 0091](specs/0091-phase4-drafter-engagement-gate.md)).

With spec 0090's parser fix exposing the underlying behaviour, run 27de's P4 was clearly showing Claude as drafter emitting STATUS: APPROVED with OPEN_ISSUES: 0 on round 1 — before reading any reviewer feedback at all (verbatim turn body: *"(No prior issues.
No new issues raised this round — the draft is the product of consensus reached in Phase 2.) Issue ledger: 0 open items."* followed by APPROVED).
He then re-emitted APPROVED/oi=0 every subsequent round he wrote successfully, never engaging with GPT's 5+ open issues.
Two coordinated mechanisms close the loophole:

Changed. test_phase4_converges_in_round_1 renamed to test_phase4_cannot_converge_in_round_1_but_converges_in_round_2 and rewritten to assert the post-spec-0091 behaviour: APPROVED in r1 is silently downgraded, agents are re-called in r2, convergence lands in r2 at the earliest.
Same pattern applied to the two resume tests in test_phase4_resume.py.
Fixed. Phase 4 round 1 could prematurely terminate via sycophantic APPROVED (spec 0091 § A).
Phase 2 already prevented round-1 agreement structurally; Phase 4 now does too.

summary: Timeline silently hid Phase 3 and Phase 4 on errored / deadlocked runs (spec 0088).
items: Timeline silently hid Phase 3 and Phase 4 on errored / deadlocked runs ([spec 0088](specs/0088-timeline-phase-omission-on-errored-runs.md)).

buildLiveTimeline() in live-data.jsx was gating the Phase 3 + Phase 4 sections on st !== 'errored' && st !== 'deadlocked', so any run that died after Phase 2 — e.g., a Phase 4 parse-failure — had its real on-disk Phase 3 draft and Phase 4 review-rounds stripped from the Timeline pane, while the Critique pane (which sources from a different code path) still showed the corresponding ledgers / review items.

The two panes disagreed. Fixed by mirroring the Phase 2 branching pattern: outer gate becomes if (ph >= 3) / if (ph >= 4), and the live-card branches are scoped explicitly to st === 'running' so a stopped-in-phase run surfaces its completed artifacts (rounds 1..cur) without a ghost streaming placeholder.
Verified on 27de (errored at P4, six P4 rounds now visible), 2c4f (deadlocked at P2, no phantom P3/P4 dividers — unchanged), and 3a4a (completed canonical fixture — unchanged).
Round-count off-by-one when stopped mid-phase (also spec 0088).

When a run died after a phase{2,4}_round_complete event landed but before round.current advanced, the Timeline's p2Rounds / p4Rounds formula (cur when ph === N) silently dropped the trailing round. 27de hit this exactly: phaseStats.phase4 has keys '1'..'6' but round.current = 5.
Both phases now compute Math.max(cur, Object.keys(phaseStats.phase{N}).length) when stopped, so the count and the completed-round loop both reflect disk reality.

summary: Fixed: Run-detail page took ~11 s to…
items: Run-detail page took ~11 s to load — /api/runs/{id} was calling SupabaseSessionData.materialize() on every request: a full paginated dump of session_files + events (rebuilt as transcript.jsonl) + attachment_blobs into a tmpdir, then re-read from disk for load_run_snapshot.

GZipMiddleware was risking SSE delivery delays — the middleware buffers chunks waiting to hit minimum_size; tiny per-event SSE payloads could be held back indefinitely.

summary: Fly proxy flap causing intermittent 30 s timeouts — spec 0079 set min_machines_running = 1 while leaving auto_stop_machines = "stop".
items: Fly proxy flap causing intermittent 30 s timeouts — spec 0079 set min_machines_running = 1 while leaving auto_stop_machines = "stop".

With two machines deployed, Fly's auto-scaler kept stopping the "extra" one because traffic was low; each stop/restart left the proxy's routing table briefly out of sync and roughly half of all incoming requests got "could not find a good candidate within 40 attempts at load balancing" from the Amsterdam edge.
Status board showed the two machines alternating between passing and critical every few minutes.
Switched to auto_stop_machines = "off" so both machines stay running permanently. ~$4–6/month extra; trivial trade-off for restoring reachability.
SPEC-0080.

summary: Hosted UI modal-load latency — clicking a card in the run-detail timeline used to spin for tens of seconds before the per-turn input bundle appeared.
items: Fixed. Hosted UI modal-load latency — clicking a card in the run-detail timeline used to spin for tens of seconds before the per-turn input bundle appeared.

Root causes: (1) min_machines_running = 0 meant the first click after idle paid a 30–60 s Python cold-start; (2) no server-side caching, so every modal re-open re-queried Supabase; (3) no GZipMiddleware, so 100 KB+ JSON bodies shipped uncompressed; (4) no Cache-Control hints, so the browser never re-used the bytes it already had.

Fix bundles all four: keep one machine warm, attach GZipMiddleware (≥ 1 KB), emit Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable on the immutable per-turn endpoints (/inputs/{key}, /searches/{key}), and add a 100-entry per-cache LRU in front of _read_input_bundle_supabase and _read_search_audit_supabase.
SPEC-0079.
Added. BoundedLRU in dual_research.ui.cache — thread-safe, count-bounded, value-agnostic (caches None correctly via a MISSING sentinel).
Used by the spec 0079 caches; reusable for any future append-only-immutable read path.

Round-N (N≥2) prompts now include a `## Standing items from prior rounds` section built from the ledger.
Convergence is now conservative: a phase terminates only when both the agent self-counters AND the system-derived ledger agree the open-set is empty.
Kill-switch built in: set DR_LEDGER_MODE=legacy in the environment to roll back.

summary: Critique data integrity — Phase 1 sections parsed, badges reconcile, markdown rendering fixed.
items: Phase 1 plan-draft cards now show real chip counts. The parser learned to recognise Phase 1 sections.
Phase 2 round-1 content re-categorised from `disagreement` to `claim`.
Timeline chip counts no longer trust the agent's self-counters as source of truth.
Critique header math reconciles.

summary: Fixed: Cost-pipeline integrity — preserve metrics on…
items: Cost-pipeline integrity — preserve metrics on resume, price the cache tier that was actually used, fold tool spend into the headline ([spec 0039](specs/0039-cost-pipeline-integrity.md)) — audit of the partner-vetting run (2026-05-16) surfaced a roughly 4× under-report in the user-facing total (metrics.json said $2.45 against a recomputed ~$9.86).
Three independent defects composed.

(1) Resume lost prior metrics. orchestrator/run.py:110 instantiated a fresh Metrics() on every session entry — no rehydrate from disk — so the final metrics.save() overwrote the pre-resume call list with only the resume-window calls.

The aggregator's fallback at ui/aggregator.py:211-215 was wired backwards: it only kicked in when metrics.json reported total_cost_usd == 0.0, so a non-zero resume-window total silently masked the rest of the run.
New Metrics.load_or_new(path) rehydrates on every session entry; D3 inverts the aggregator's priority so the transcript is now the primary truth and metrics.json is the cold-start fallback.

(2) Cache writes priced at the 5-minute rate when the agent requested 1h. anthropic_agent.py:30 has requested cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"} (via the extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11 beta) since spec 0017, but pricing.py:31 hardcoded cache_write_per_mtok = 3.75 — the 1.25× = 5-minute rate.
Anthropic bills 1h writes at 2× input.

ModelPricing now splits cache_write_5m_per_mtok (1.25× input) and cache_write_1h_per_mtok (2× input); TokenUsage gains cache_write_5m_tokens + cache_write_1h_tokens (the aggregate cache_write_tokens stays as the sum for back-compat on the transcript wire shape); the Anthropic agent reads usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens / ephemeral_1h_input_tokens and prices each tier exactly.
New run multi-round phases now bill correctly — old transcripts can't be retroactively re-attributed because they only carried the aggregate field.
(3) Web-search fees missing from every persisted total. Spec 0031 D7 had carved search_cost out as a side-channel surfaced only in the Consumption tab's expanded panel.
With (1) and (2) fixed, the gap between the headline and the invoice became obvious.

New canonical compute_full_cost(model_id, usage, searches) is what stamps every persisted cost_usd (AgentResult, TurnEnded, CallRecord, metrics.json total, RunCompleted, Supabase runs.total_cost_usd); compute_token_cost is the renamed-but-preserved per-token helper, used for the breakdown ("of which tokens / of which web search").
TurnEnded event shape gains cache_write_5m_tokens / cache_write_1h_tokens / search_cost.
TurnTokenUsage gains token_cost (= cost − search_cost, invariant).
The Consumption tab relabels its "tool cost" line to "of which web search" — clear that it's a breakdown, not a separate charge.

(4) Transcript dedup by label. Parse-error recoveries replay the same turn_ended label multiple times; the partner-vetting run had every phase4-r*-* label appearing twice (the naive transcript sum was $12.74; the deduped sum is $8.78).
load_run_snapshot pre-filters the event stream to keep only the last occurrence per label; _sum_transcript_cost and the recompute tool follow the same convention.
Sibling labels (phase4-r1-claude and phase4-r1-claude-repair) are NOT deduped — they're distinct API calls billed separately, and the agent-level rollup includes both.

(5) New dual-research recompute-costs --run RUN_ID | --all [--push] [--dry-run] subcommand. Re-walks each run's transcript, recomputes every per-turn cost under the new pricing rules (folds search in; old transcripts get 5m attribution for cache writes since the per-TTL split was never recorded), rewrites metrics.json, and backs up the original to metrics.json.pre-0039.bak on the first invocation (idempotent — re-runs preserve the original-original).
All existing local runs backfilled; runs.total_cost_usd on Supabase will be updated post-deploy via recompute-costs --all --push.
(6) UI breakdown. CostBadge tooltip shows ${cost} (tokens $X · web search $Y) when searchCost > 0.
The CLI [run] summary line gains the same breakdown when search fees fired.
Note: totals on the run list & detail header will INCREASE for runs that used web search or 1h-cache writes — the partner-vetting run's headline jumped from $2.45 to $9.86.

22 new tests across pricing (per-TTL splits, compute_full_cost invariants, snapshot table), persistence (CallRecord shape, Metrics.load_or_new rehydrate + missing file + corrupt JSON + old-shape tolerance), aggregator (transcript-primary fallback, dedup by label, search-fee fold-in for pre-spec events), and tests/audit/test_recompute.py (dedup, idempotence, backup-once, dry-run, --all walks directory). 602 total green.

summary: Added: Consumption-tab follow-ups — tier-lookup window, click-to-expand…
items: Consumption-tab follow-ups — tier-lookup window, click-to-expand bars, per-phase web-search count ([spec 0031](specs/0031-consumption-followups.md)) — three concerns from first-pass testing of the spec-0030 Consumption tab.
(1) 1M context window for old runs. Spec 0030's RunStarted.{agent}_context_window fields fixed fresh runs only — older transcripts replayed at 200K / 128K because they didn't carry the field.
The aggregator now derives the right window server-side by scanning config.TIERS for any ModelSpec whose model_id matches the run's recorded agent model.
claude-sonnet-4-6 → PROD_TIER.claude.context_window → 1,000,000.
Every existing prod-tier run renders at 1M immediately on the next deploy with zero data migration.
Same fallback applied per-turn for defence in depth (handles the theoretical edge where run_started was never seen).

(2) Click-to-expand bars. ConsumptionRow is now clickable; clicking toggles an expanded body below it that lays out the per-piece breakdown as an explicit 3-column table — kind label · Claude tokens · OpenAI tokens — with renormalised numbers matching what each bar's segments depict.
Rows summarising input total, output, web searches, and tool cost sit beneath.
The legend gains a hint: *click any phase row to see exact per-input numbers*.
Multiple rows can be expanded independently; click again to collapse.
(3) Per-phase web-search count + cost. Originally pitched as "tokens used by tools" — but neither provider reports tool tokens separately (search results fold into input_tokens).
The honest substitute is the per-turn search-request count, which AgentResult.extras["searches"] already captured but no event threaded forward.
TurnEnded.searches now carries it; TurnTokenUsage gains searches + search_cost (computed via a new ModelPricing.web_search_per_request rate — $0.010/req for Claude, $0.025/req for the GPT-5 family).
Search cost is a separate side-channel — does NOT join compute_cost (which stays strictly token-cost), so the headline cost chip keeps its existing semantics.

The expanded row shows web searches + tool cost per lane only when at least one lane had a search in that turn, avoiding clutter for non-search phases. 18 new tests covering pricing rates + compute_search_cost, aggregator wiring for searches / search_cost, the TIERS lookup fallback (with unknown-model fall-through), and wire-format presence of all new fields. 424 total green.

summary: Timeline UX pass — inline unfold, per-input consumption segments, real context windows, parser repairs (spec 0030) — five UI / data follow-ups to spec 0029 packed into one pass.
items: Timeline UX pass — inline unfold, per-input consumption segments, real context windows, parser repairs ([spec 0030](specs/0030-timeline-ux-pass.md)) — five UI / data follow-ups to spec 0029 packed into one pass.
(1) Inline unfold. Clicking a timeline card no longer opens the modal directly.
Instead the card unfolds in place to show a synthesised gist line (e.g.
Claude still negotiating, raised 4 questions, conceded a held D-N.), the ## Summary TL;DR, and a new View in full mode button — that button is now the only entry into ArtifactModal.
Live items skip the toggle (they still stream inline).

(2 + 3) Disagreement parser fallback. _parse_one_entry in ui/disagreements.py gained a heading-only fallback: when no (a) D-N: "…" sub-bullet exists, it walks the block, skips meta prefixes (status:, > quote:, > after:, - > quote:), and takes the first content line as point (capped at 200 chars with … truncation).
The same pass picks up I claim: / They claim: bullets for my_position / other_position.
The Disagreements panel now renders an actual contested-point sentence; progression timeline entries show "raised <point>" instead of bare "raised".

(4) Per-input consumption segments. The Consumption-tab bars now decompose into one coloured segment per prompt-piece kind in the Tk palette (brief / d1 / d2 / plan / hist / draft / histp) — the same vocabulary as the ChatLifecycle chips on the how-it-works page.

Each phase orchestrator computes piece sizes from its input strings at call time via a new protocol/prompt_pieces.py helper (single char÷3.5 heuristic for both providers; provider's reported input_tokens is the cost-of-record, piece widths are renormalised to sum to it).
Pieces ride the TurnEnded event in a new prompt_pieces: dict[str, int] field; aggregator preserves them on TurnTokenUsage.prompt_pieces.
(5) Real context windows. agents/context_windows.py (introduced in spec 0029 with hand-rolled values) is deleted.
RunStarted now carries claude_context_window and openai_context_window, sourced from the tier's ModelSpec.context_window (1M for PROD_TIER; 200K / 400K for TEST_TIER).

The aggregator stamps them on AgentState.context_window and on each TurnTokenUsage.context_window; the frontend reads the bar denominator straight off the wire — prod-tier runs now display 1M-token-wide bars for both lanes. 25 new tests (prompt-pieces shapes per phase + renormalise + zero-history edge cases; aggregator wiring for both context_window and prompt_pieces; wire-format roundtrip including camelised inner keys; disagreement parser fallback for heading-only / bullet-meta / label-echo / inline-precedence cases). 406 total green.

summary: Added: Token-consumption tab — per-turn context-window visualisation…
items: Token-consumption tab — per-turn context-window visualisation ([spec 0029](specs/0029-token-consumption-tab.md)) — the timeline pane on a run-detail view now carries a two-pill segmented control on the left of its toolbar: Conversation (existing card view, unchanged) and Consumption (new).
The two per-agent total chips that used to sit at the left of the toolbar move to the right end.

Switching to Consumption swaps the artifact-card list out for a 3-column grid — phase / round label · Claude lane · OpenAI lane — borrowed verbatim from the ChatLifecycle visual on the how-it-works page.

Each row is one API call (one turn per round per agent); P0 / P1 / P3 give a single row each, Phase 2 and Phase 4 give one row per round per agent, so the visual makes the buildup explicit — round 3 of Phase 2 is visibly larger than round 1 because the conversation history grew.

Each bar is sized to its model's actual context window (Claude 200K, GPT-5.5 200K, GPT-5-mini 128K, default 128K for unknown ids) sourced from a new dual_research/agents/context_windows.py registry; the percent number under each bar gives the apples-to-apples comparison when the two lanes have different denominators.
Bars have three layers: cache-read portion (lighter shade, ≤ input), fresh input (full agent colour), and a thinner output tail (darker shade, 60% height).
Hover any bar for the full breakdown (input · cache read · output · cache write · cost · model id).

The new TurnTokenUsage dataclass + Run.phase_token_usage flat dict captures the per-turn detail in the aggregator from TurnEnded events (which already carried input_tokens / output_tokens / cache_read_tokens / cache_write_tokens / cost_usd / model_id — the data was being discarded before this spec).

Keys use the existing phase{N}_ / phase{N}_round{R}_ convention that phase_summaries and phase_review_items already use; the wire-format camelizer rewrites them to phase{N}{Agent} / phase{N}Round{R}{Agent} (e.g.
phase2Round1Claude).

Runs replayed from pre-0029 transcripts have an empty dict; the Consumption tab shows a small "no per-turn data" empty state. 17 new tests (per-phase key shapes, payload roundtrip, accumulation preservation, registry coverage, wire-format inner-key + field-name camelisation). 389 total green.

summary: Cross-review inline comments — Phase 4 side-by-side modal (spec 0028) — final spec on the visualisation track.
items: Cross-review inline comments — Phase 4 side-by-side modal ([spec 0028](specs/0028-review-inline-comments.md)) — final spec on the visualisation track.

Clicking a Phase 4 turn card now opens the same side-by-side modal as Phase 2: left pane is the current converged document, right pane is the agent's issues / comments / disagreements as anchored cards.
Click a card → left pane scrolls + flashes; > after: cards mount a dashed "insert here" ghost block.

The aggregator picks the highest-numbered phase4/draft-v*.md if drafter revisions have landed, else falls back to phase3/draft-v1.md, and surfaces the result as Run.current_draft_path (camelCase currentDraftPath at the wire).

review_turn_prompt gains the same one-paragraph anchor hint under ## Issue ledger, ## Comments on the current draft, and ## Substantive disagreements I'm holding — asking each numbered item / D-N entry to carry an optional > quote: or > after: blockquote sub-line.

The extract_review_items parser learns two new section recognisers (## Issue ledger (delta + currently open) and ## Comments on the current draft); existing recognisers (Open questions, Substantive disagreements, Resolved or non-blocking, Final-surfaced, Round-1 diff) keep their behaviour.
The aggregator's _read_phase_review_items walks Phase 4 round files too, keyed as phase4_round{R}_ — same shape as Phase 2's keys.

The frontend dispatches both statsPhase === 2 and statsPhase === 4 turn cards to NegotiateReviewModal; priorContentPathFor returns run.currentDraftPath for Phase 4 items and the existing other-agent prior turn for Phase 2.

Phase 3 (single-shot drafting) and the final document stay single-pane — no critique sections to anchor. 13 new tests covering Phase 4 parser shapes, Phase 4 prompt marker presence in all three sections, aggregator keying, current_draft_path resolution (highest revision wins, falls back to phase3, null when neither exists), and wire-format presence of currentDraftPath. 372 total green.

summary: Added: Negotiate inline comments — side-by-side modal…
items: Negotiate inline comments — side-by-side modal with anchored critique cards ([spec 0027](specs/0027-negotiate-inline-comments.md)) — second of three specs on the visualisation track, completing the Google-Docs-/GitHub-PR-style review experience for Phase 2 (negotiation) turns.
Renumbered from the original "0026" plan after PR #26 took that slot for the how-it-works restructure.

Clicking a Phase 2 turn card now opens a side-by-side modal: left pane (60%) shows the prior content being critiqued — the OTHER agent's most recent turn for round N≥2, or their Phase 1 draft for round 1 — rendered through the spec-0025 Markdown component with stable b- ids on every block.

Right pane (40%) shows the agent's questions, disagreements, and resolved items as inline-comment cards, grouped by kind with colour-coded left rails (questions = info-blue, disagreements = warn-amber, resolved = ok-green, missing = dashed amber).
Clicking a card scrolls the left pane to the referenced span and applies a 1.5s amber-fade highlight; > after: cards mount a dashed-ghost "insert here" placeholder under the anchored heading.
j / k (or ↓ / ↑) walk between cards, Enter re-jumps the active card, Esc closes the modal.

The anchoring data comes from a one-paragraph prompt addition in both negotiation_round1_prompt and negotiation_turn_prompt asking each numbered question and D-N disagreement to carry an optional > quote: or > after: blockquote sub-line.

A new extract_review_items parser in protocol/parse.py walks the four anchored sections (Open questions / Substantive disagreements / Resolved or non-blocking / Final-surfaced) and returns a flat list[ReviewItem]; the aggregator surfaces these as Run.phase_review_items keyed by phase2_round{R}_.
Un-anchored items still render — they just don't auto-jump, so older runs without the marker convention degrade gracefully.
Anchor resolution is two-step: hash-id lookup (using the stable ids 0025 already emits), then case-insensitive substring fallback across the left pane's rendered blocks.
The frontend keeps the existing single-pane modal for Phase 1 plan drafts, Phase 3 converged document, and the final document; spec 0028 layers the side-by-side onto Phase 4 (cross-review).

New scrollAndFlash helper in shared.jsx (works for any container/blockId/text/afterHeading combination, reusable in 0028). 16 new tests covering parser shapes, prompt-marker presence, aggregator wiring, and key shapes. 359 total green.

summary: How-it-works restructure — chat-lifecycle diagram, phase accordions, v3.5 process map (spec 0026) — UI-only refresh of #/how-it-works.
items: How-it-works restructure — chat-lifecycle diagram, phase accordions, v3.5 process map ([spec 0026](specs/0026-howitworks-redesign.md)) — UI-only refresh of #/how-it-works.

The page now opens with a four-card TL;DR strip (models · stateless transport · parallel timing · mechanical convergence), and the phase-by-phase walkthrough is collapsed into expandable accordions, each carrying an Inputs / Chats / Output / Gate / Caps meta block.

New Chat lifecycle section addresses the most-asked question about the protocol — when do we start new chats? — with a 3-column grid (phase · Claude lane · OpenAI lane) showing every API call across all five phases, with the exact context bundle inside each call rendered as colour-coded chips (brief, P1 draft-claude, P1 draft-openai, P2 turns, agreed plan, current draft, P4 turns); a legend underneath maps the chip colours, and a side-by-side "what we don't do (×) / what we actually do (✓)" panel calls out the absence of any thread_id, OpenAI Assistants API, or persistent state.

A new Context grows, but the prefix is cached stacked-bar visual makes the CACHE_BREAKPOINT cost story concrete — showing how the prompt grows from brief only (P0/P1) to brief + 2 drafts + 4/10 P2 turns (P2 r3/r6) through to the full P3 drafter context, with the cache split point marked on the axis.

FAQ entries become individually-collapsible
blocks.

New View full process map fold-out under the phase strip embeds the v3.5 protocol landscape (Phase 0 → Phase 4 → Final Document) with source-verification / repair / exit-code callouts and the protocol's principles footer — authored via the diagram skill (cream-and-indigo, Inter, 1660×880, no animations) and shipped both inlined inside how-it-works.jsx and as a standalone src/dual_research/ui/static/protocol-overview.svg for download.

The inline visuals (phase strip, chat-lifecycle grid, context bars, round-up-close diagram) remain theme-aware via the existing --agent-a / --agent-b tokens; the fold-out map is the explicit exception — a separate reference surface that stays light regardless of the chrome bar's theme toggle.
No backend changes, no prompt changes, no wire-format changes — the page just stopped under-selling what the orchestrator already does.

summary: Added: Visualisation foundations — modal pattern, summary…
items: Visualisation foundations — modal pattern, summary cards, preflight tabs, attachment ingest ([spec 0025](specs/0025-visualisation-foundations.md)) — first of three specs building toward a Google-Docs-/GitHub-PR-style review experience across the run timeline.

Replaces the inline expand-in-place behaviour on every timeline card with a summary card that shows a TL;DR + the same stats row, plus a "View full" button that opens a big centred modal with a dimmed overlay.
The TL;DR comes from each agent's existing ## Summary (or ## Summary of position) section that the protocol already requires; no prompt changes.
The aggregator now extracts these into Run.phaseSummaries keyed by phase{N}_ / phase{N}_round{R}_, plus a briefSummary heuristic from brief.md for the preflight card.
The preflight modal is tabbed (Content / Sources / Files).

Attachments are now first-class in ingest: a new Attachment dataclass + attachments.py module captures images, PDFs, files, and links from markdown, Notion blocks (image / pdf / file / bookmark / embed / link_preview / rich-text hrefs), and a new repeatable --attach VALUE CLI flag (local path or URL).
Local files are hashed and copied into /attachments/-; the index lives in /attachments.json.

Hosted runs get a new supabase/migrations/0003_attachment_blobs.sql table that stores base64-encoded binary blobs; --push upserts both the JSON index (via session_files) and the blobs; the supabase datasource restores binaries byte-for-byte on materialise.
Two new server endpoints: GET /api/runs/{id}/attachments (parsed JSON index) and GET /api/runs/{id}/attachment-blobs/{rel_path} (serves binary with the recorded MIME, path-traversal-guarded).

Markdown rendering gets hash-stable block ids on every paragraph / heading / list item / blockquote / code — same text → same id="b-" across re-renders, ready for spec 0026's inline-comments anchoring.
New Modal component in shared.jsx (overlay + Esc + tab strip), and the front-end's Markdown component runs every parse through _injectBlockIds.
Side-by-side inline comments for phase 2 / 3 / 4 are out of scope here and land in 0026 + 0027.

summary: Changed: Run-detail header pass 2 + compact…
items: Run-detail header pass 2 + compact theme toggle ([spec 0024](specs/0024-header-pass-2-theme-toggle.md)) — strip the redundant back-chip text (icon-only back arrow now), the dual-research brand pill, the gradient icon, and the copy-id chip.
Topic gets a "TOPIC" caps tag.

summary: Compact run-detail header, "How it works" page, and release notes (spec 0023) — three bundled UX changes.
items: Compact run-detail header, "How it works" page, and release notes ([spec 0023](specs/0023-header-howitworks-notes.md)) — three bundled UX changes.

The run-detail header drops from four vertical rows to two: one primary row with back chip, merged dual-research/run-id pill, single-line topic, phase progress dots, phase label, cost, status, and a compact errors badge; one subtle mono meta row with started/drafter/elapsed/outcome (and in-flight round when applicable).
Recovers about one timeline-card height.

New "How it works" link in the chrome bar (right of the connection pill) opens a static page at #/how-it-works that walks through the protocol end-to-end: brief ingestion, the five phases with parallelism hints, hand-rolled inline SVGs of the phase flow and a single negotiation round, an FAQ covering "who goes first" (no-one — both agents fire via asyncio.gather), "fresh chats or one long chat" (fresh per turn; CACHE_BREAKPOINT is prefix caching, not a session), the tiebreak cascade, soft/hard cap behaviour, repair semantics.
Release notes embedded as a VERSION_NOTES array seeded with v0.18 → v0.22 entries; CONTRIBUTING.md asks future user-visible specs to append a new entry there.
New Icon.Help glyph.
Static-only frontend work; no backend changes.

summary: Admin allowlist UI + profile menu + landing-page redesign (spec 0022) — wraps up the hosted-deployment track with three user-facing upgrades.
items: Admin allowlist UI + profile menu + landing-page redesign ([spec 0022](specs/0022-admin-and-polish.md)) — wraps up the hosted-deployment track with three user-facing upgrades.

New admin route at #/settings (table of allowlist rows, inline add with optional admin checkbox, per-row remove) backed by four new endpoints: GET /api/me (email, isAdmin, avatarUrl, fullName from Google), GET/POST /api/approved-emails, DELETE /api/approved-emails/{email} — all admin-gated, with server-side protection against self-delete and removing the last admin (409 with a human-readable message).

SupabaseAuthMiddleware now plumbs is_admin through the scope so admin handlers don't need a second DB lookup. 13 new unit tests; total 277.

summary: Added: Google OAuth + email allowlist via…
items: Google OAuth + email allowlist via Supabase Auth ([spec 0021](specs/0021-google-oauth.md)) — the hosted UI now authenticates users via Google OAuth (mediated by Supabase Auth) and gates every /api/* request through an approved_emails allowlist.
The HTTP Basic auth stopgap from spec 0020 is removed.
New supabase/migrations/0002_approved_emails.sql defines the allowlist table and seeds the project owner as the first admin.
New SupabaseAuthMiddleware validates Bearer tokens via client.auth.get_user(token) and checks the email against the allowlist, with a 60s in-memory cache keyed on token hash.
/api/health and a new /api/config (returns supabaseUrl + supabaseAnonKey for the browser bootstrap) bypass the gate.
Frontend gains auth.jsx (Supabase JS SDK bootstrap, useSession hook, sign-in screen, not-approved screen, top-level authedFetch).

Local dual-research serve (RUNS_BACKEND=fs) is never auth-gated. 10 new unit tests; 7 basic-auth tests removed.
Total: 264.

summary: Added: Fly.io deployment of the UI server…
items: Fly.io deployment of the UI server with Supabase-backed aggregator ([spec 0020](specs/0020-fly-deploy.md)) — the dual-research serve UI server can now run on Fly.io against the Supabase tables that spec 0019 introduced, so pushed runs are visible at a public URL.
New RUNS_BACKEND=fs|supabase env var picks the backend at server boot — defaults to fs so local invocations are unchanged.

In supabase mode, /api/runs queries the runs table directly (with a second query for brief.md topics) and the /api/runs/{id} + /stream paths materialize a tmp directory from session_files + events on each request, then hand it to the existing aggregator unchanged.
New Dockerfile (python:3.14-slim, uv-managed deps) + .dockerignore + fly.toml (region iad, shared-cpu-1x@256mb, auto-stop after idle, health-check on /api/health).
New BasicAuthMiddleware gates every route when UI_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD is set (Fly secret); /api/health always bypasses the gate so Fly's prober can see the machine.

summary: Supabase schema + `--push` CLI.

summary: Added: Hosted deployment kickoff handoff package (spec…
items: Hosted deployment kickoff handoff package ([spec 0018](specs/0018-hosted-deployment-kickoff.md)) — new document handoffs/hosted-deployment-kickoff.md bootstrapping a multi-session track that takes dual-research from a local tool to a publicly accessible, Google-auth-gated, DB-backed hosted UI.

Locks in architectural decisions (Fly.io for hosting, Supabase for Postgres + Google OAuth + email allowlist, orchestrator stays local and pushes session data via a new CLI subcommand), spells out why Fly was chosen over Vercel (incompatibility between Vercel's serverless model and the current watchfiles + SSE backend; future kickoff-from-UI's 8–15-minute compute), enumerates the spec roadmap (0019 DB schema + push CLI, 0020 Fly deploy, 0021 Google OAuth + allowlist, 0022 admin route, 0023 later kickoff-from-UI), lists pre-work the user must do (Supabase project + credentials, Fly CLI install), surfaces open design questions for spec 0019, and ships a paste-ready prompt for a fresh Claude Code session to start the new track.
Documentation only; backend and UI unchanged at v0.16.2 behaviour. 223 tests still green.

summary: Deadlocked phase-2 last round (spec 0017) — when a run deadlocked at the Phase 2 hard cap, the timeline rendered N-1 of N turn-card pairs.
items: Deadlocked phase-2 last round ([spec 0017](specs/0017-deadlock-last-round.md)) — when a run deadlocked at the Phase 2 hard cap, the timeline rendered N-1 of N turn-card pairs.
The Phase 2 in-progress branch computed completedThrough = cur - 1, expecting the live branch below to cover the cur round — but the live branch only fired for status === 'running'.
For deadlocked / errored, the cur round was on disk and complete but neither branch picked it up.

summary: Added: Anthropic prompt caching (spec 0006) —…
items: Added. Anthropic prompt caching ([spec 0006](specs/0006-prompt-caching.md)) — every phase prompt (except repair_prompt) now includes a CACHE_BREAKPOINT sentinel at the boundary between the stable prefix and the dynamic per-call suffix.

ClaudeAgent detects the marker, splits the content into two text blocks, attaches cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"} to the prefix, and adds the extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11 beta header for 1-hour cache lifetime.
GptAgent strips the marker (OpenAI Responses API caches prefixes automatically).
DUAL_RESEARCH_NO_CACHE=1 disables caching on both providers.
Cost ticker now shows cache:r/w when nonzero.
Verified live: single-call A/B showed 76.6% savings on the second identical call (5,550 tokens cache-written then cache-read at $0.10/M vs $1/M input). 12 new pytest cases; total: 93 green.

Fixed. Cross-round cache invalidation in Phase 2 / Phase 4 prompts. The round-specific header (# Phase 2 round {round}...) used to sit BEFORE the cache breakpoint inside negotiation_turn_prompt / review_turn_prompt, which changed the cached prefix hash on every round → no cross-round cache hits, only within-round.
Restructured both builders so the round number is referenced AFTER the breakpoint.
Verified by full Phase 0→4 E2E on test tier: agents converged to APPROVED in Phase 4 round 3, 23 model calls, $0.79 total, cache reads visible across rounds.

Anthropic 30K-tokens/min rate limit still bites prod-tier multi-round Phase 2 around round 6. Caching halved per-call input cost but cache _writes_ (the dynamic suffix that grows each round) still count against the per-minute input quota.
Spec 0007 will add rate-limit-aware backoff + resume-from-prior-session so partial runs are recoverable.
